#4081. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#4080. Genshin Impact Luna 5 takes the squad back to Mondstadt, finally makes Varka playable

Genshin Impact's next update will have you reminiscing about the good ol' days of... 2020.

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

Nioh 3 has taken the Nioh franchise to new heights, delivering its biggest-ever launch.

#4078. More Delays Hit MTG Reality Fracture Secret Lair Bundle Right Before Shipping

More shipping woes strike Wizards of the Coast even after all the sets for 2026 have been released.

Delay woes just keep coming for Magic: The Gathering, as fresh delays have hit a recent Secret Lair drop just two days before shipping was due to begin in North America.

In an email sent to some buyers of the Reality Fracture Secret Lair bundle, Wizards of the Coast has confirmed that the planned shipping date of November 19 is now being moved to December 16, almost an entire month after shipping was due to begin.

There are also delays for those in Europe and the UK, which we'll get to, but those orders were already on a later schedule.

The email Wizards of the Coast sent to customers today is, for many, the final straw. Delays and cancellations have been the story of the year in Magic, and it's marred what should have been an otherwise hugely successful year for the game, but the discourse around overprinting products and Wizards biting off more than it can chew has completely dominated the narrative towards the end of the year.

Star Trek stock is still massively delayed for some retailers, meaning pre-orders and back orders still haven't been fulfilled. Total Cards in the UK today reached out to customers to confirm that virtually every product is still delayed in some form.

With the Reality Fracture Secret Lair bundle, however, customers purchased this product under the guise that stock would be sent out relatively quickly, and the planned shipping date of November 19 for North America has been moved to December 16 with 48 hours' notice. The email states that customers can still opt to cancel or amend their orders, but some on Reddit report that payment has already been taken, making it harder to do so.

Elsewhere, the Reality Fracture Secret Lair products were due to ship on December 29 for Europe and the UK, but this has now been shifted to January 19, 2027. This is particularly alarming, as it's just two weeks before the Nauctis: The Sunken Realm prerelease, sparking fears that this latest delay will impact future sets and give 2027 a poor start in terms of availability.

Every set of 2026 has had availability issues in some form, with the problems getting gradually more severe to the point where Star Trek has to cancel the planned beginner box, and some retailers still haven't had their full orders delivered almost two weeks after prerelease.

The lack of transparency around why these issues have been happening is what is stressing players out the most, and while some reasons have been sprinkled in here and there, many announcements are hidden on the Daily MTG feed and are bare-bones statements that confirm the delays rather than explain them. Meanwhile, there's yet another Secret Lair drop happening right now, in addition to last week's Star Trek one.

It really calls into question the business strategy to have so many releases in one year; when you can't meet demand, why wasn't the decision made to slow things down?

Could we see a James Bond Secret Lair, or even a full set, following a teasing Instagram comment after Robert Pattinson's casting confirmation?

#4077. The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

Maxis has offered some fresh details on its long-running mission to improve player quality of life in The Sims 4.

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

The 336-page book launches in Japan on 9th February 2027 and will be available from both the region's online storefront and the official Nintendo Stores across Japan for 3,960 yen (around £19 / $25).

It's apparently rammed with over 5,000 pieces of concept art from the game, divided into five chapters focused on the artwork, creatures, style, and world, with a mysterious 'bonus' section at the end.

It's all still a work in progress at the moment, but Nintendo has shared a handful of sample pages online, which we have grouped together for you to check out below:

Splatoon Raiders is one of the most stylish games we've seen from Nintendo this year, so it makes sense that it would get the full art book treatment soon enough. We're keeping our fingers crossed that it doesn't stay a Japanese exclusive for too long.

#4075. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4074. I Wish Had Spoken To Reid Duke Before I Started Playing Magic: The Gathering

We spoke with MTG Hall of Famer Reid Duke about how new players should approach Magic and how it's different now than when he started playing.

Few names are as iconic as Reid Duke in Magic: The Gathering. Picking up the game at just five years old, Reid Duke went on to win the Magic Online World Championship in 2011, six Grand Prix events, and one Pro Tour. Still active in the competitive scene and helping teach the next generation of Magic players, Reid Duke is currently part of team TCGplayer, and when they extended the opportunity to chat with one of the game's legends, it was the fastest I've ever responded to an email.

Fast-forward to our chat, and Reid was exactly as many have already stated: a gentleman. He is easily the nicest person I've ever had the pleasure of interviewing, but better still, he's a fount of knowledge when it comes to Magic, and specifically how new players should approach the game. During our chat, we focused heavily on new players and their progression from discovering the game to picking a preferred format, and everything in between. Here are the highlights from our chat, which includes some advice I desperately wish I'd had when I first discovered Magic over 15 years ago!

The first question I asked Reid was about new players finding their way into Magic. I used my own story as an example: when I first discovered Magic, I had access to cards from a local comic shop, but no LGS to play at, and finding that environment was tough. The only LGS I knew of basically rejected me because I was new, and everyone else was a long-time player who didn't want to teach me. Thankfully, most LGS communities are far more accepting of new players now, and I've always made sure that any store I play at treats all players the same regardless of how long they've played the game. Still, with paper, Online, and MTG Arena as routes into the game, here's what Reid had to say on new players finding their way into Magic:

"I think Arena is a great tool, there are so many ways to engage with Magic, and there's not necessarily a right or a wrong way, but for a new player who doesn't even know how they prefer to engage with Magic, the first thing I would recommend is Arena, because it is so quick, so easy, so accessible. You don't have to put yourself out on a limb in terms of travel, research, or feeling embarrassed to learn the rules of the game in front of experienced players, so there's no beating Arena in terms of accessibility, and it's a really great platform for learning the rules."

Reid would go on to point out the obvious, which is that when he first engaged with Magic, there was no Magic Online or MTG Arena; all he had were the physical cards and the more personal approach of learning the game through making connections with other players, and that route is still extremely valid today, but I completely agree with his point on Arena being far more accessible and, most importantly in the current economy, free.

Four Commander precons for Nauctis: The Sunken Realm have appeared online, and there are some very interesting archetypes in play.

The next question I put to Reid was about Wizards' new-player agenda, and whether it was doing enough to consistently bring new players in and keep them playing. His response was a little unexpected in that, for someone who has been playing for so long, to acknowledge the challenge of getting into Magic due to the core rules is something I figured would be second nature to him now. Here is his full response:

"I think Wizards do a great job of a few things: first, making the best game in the world, but also providing a variety of formats, products and opportunities for players of every level. The biggest obstacle to new player acquisition in Magic is that it's a very challenging game. The rules are hard, and even the most popular casual format, Commander, is very, very complicated, and you encounter a lot of complicated new cards very quickly. New players should be aware that you're going to encounter some challenging stuff as you're learning Magic, but try to be patient and don't get intimidated by that. However, if you manage to get your hands on a beginner box or Foundations kit, you're going to learn the basics a bit quicker, and you can get to the harder mechanics as and when you're ready for them."

I personally didn't consider Magic a complicated game until I started playing games like Lorcana and Riftbound long after I already had Magic pretty much sussed out, but to hear from a 30+ year pro that the game is hard is somewhat validating of those early struggles and should make every player feel better about where they are in their Magic journey.

Now that we've covered some of the routes into Magic and how Wizards is doing at getting new players into the game, I wanted to know where Reid believes new players should go next. Over his career, Reid has played pretty much every format out there at least once (I imagine), but obviously we'd focus on a few core formats as the next step. Here's the advice he has on where new players should look for their first big format commitment:

"Once someone gets their feet underneath them, they've experienced Magic and learned the rules, I would really encourage them to just feel it out and go where the game takes them, and go to the format that's the most fun for them. Now, I will say that my first recommendation for basically anyone is to try Limited. Sealed deck or booster draft, some of the advantages of Limited are that it's a totally even playing field, it's affordable as you don't need a huge collection to get into it, and it's really strong for emphasizing the fundamentals of the game and rules. I think anyone can have fun with Limited, and from there, it's a branching path where, if you have a competitive itch, you will probably go to Standard next, or if your preference leads you to casual Commander, at and LGS or even the kitchen table, that is a super popular way to engage with Magic as well."

This is, and I mean this with zero hyperbole, phenomenal advice. I started playing Limited and prerelease events only in the last few years, and I've become a far better Magic player because of it, but Limited felt intimidating at first. Opening packs and building a deck seemed daunting, but Reid is absolutely right: it's the best and most logical next step once you've grasped the basics.

I genuinely wish someone had given me this advice 15 years ago, because my whole relationship with the game would be completely different, but hopefully, in having this discussion with Reid, there's at least one player out there who will now feel confident enough to just tackle Limited as soon as they're ready, to see where the game takes them next.

When talking a little more about Limited specifically, Reid would expand further on his thoughts surrounding new players engaging with the format.

"Make no mistake, booster draft is played on the Pro Tour at the very highest level, so it's a challenging, deep, engaging format, but I do really strongly believe that it's fun for players at every level, it's a great way to build your collection, learn the rules, and make friends. I would love to highlight prerelease as a really great entry point for players, especially if it's their first time showing up to an LGS and playing with real opponents, because a prerelease is the definition of an even playing field."

As a father actively teaching his daughter to play Magic, I've found the game can be really good for critical and strategic thinking, but it's also a great way to teach reading comprehension and even math. I asked Reid, as someone who started playing at just five years old, whether there is, or should be, a barrier to entry for Magic directly linked to age.

"No barrier to entry. At this point I've taught hundreds of people magic in my lifetime and I have not met someone of any age or background who could not have something to enjoy or learn from Magic."

It's great to hear that Reid is giving back to the game in the form of teaching new players, but even better to hear that he is also of the belief that, if someone wants to learn how to play, there really is no limit that should be applied when it comes to age or background.

I believe there is a ton of value in Magic as a teaching tool. While I've already mentioned that I'm teaching my daughter to play, she has dyslexia, and that can make reading the cards quite tricky, so I try to use the game to aid her reading comprehension and support her already impressive math skills. Granted, this gets much harder when she starts sending an army of goblins to kill me via the Krenko deck she plays with, but that's a small price to pay for the potential upside of engaging her brain with the game.

One final question I had for Reid about new players was around the color pie, and again I pulled from my own experiences with Magic: when I first started playing, I always drifted toward Dimir (black-blue) decks. This was partly because it was the first deck I ever built, the first deck that got me to Mythic on Arena, and the first deck guide I ever wrote on a personal blog.

Over time, I've had to work hard to pull myself away from Dimir decks as a preference in Limited and Standard because it sometimes felt like I was forcing an archetype that wasn't powerful in the moment.

So, I asked Reid whether he has ever struggled with the same issue of color preference, and what his advice would be for new players entering the game.

"Everyone has a preference, one of the great things about Magic is that you can express yourself creatively in deckbuilding and the cards that you choose. My favorite colors are black and green. On the other hand, some of my biggest level up moments as a competitive player and some of my richest experiences in terms of having fun with the game, have been when my friends and teammates have encouraged me to go outside my comfort zone. As a competitive player, you want to go with whatever strategy you believe is best and will give you the chance to achieve your goals, but for anyone at any level, there's no wrong way to do it. Have your preferences, do what's fun for you, just be willing to challenge yourself and go outside of your comfort zone."

It is almost comforting to hear from such an accomplished player that they still need to be pushed outside their comfort zone, and it probably validates the idea that having a preference within the game is completely healthy, provided you're having fun.

Reid was incredible to talk to, and we'll have another part to this interview coming later this week, focusing on the wider game of magic and competitive play.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4073. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

VR horror could soon become a lot more frightening

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sony has filed a patent that sounds like it could make VR horror gaming terrifyingly more immersive.

According to a report from Patentlyze, Sony Interactive Entertainment has filed a patent for a curved neckband that would "supply air to one or more of the neck and a part above the neck of the user; and control the air blowing devices based on the control signal."

In schematics from Sony's patent application, a drawing of a person is seen wearing the neckband alongside a VR headset, suggesting the device is intended as an accessory to the PSVR 2 or a potential successor. If the patent ultimately manifests as a real, wearable product, Sony says it'll come with "a communication unit configured to receive a control signal from an external apparatus," likely meaning it connects to your console to receive instruction on when to activate.

Speaking of which, Sony's patent describes the collar as being outfitted with "a plurality of air blowing devices configured to supply air to the neck or a part above the neck of the user." So, the face? The chin? The air will blow "based on the control signal received" from the unit, suggesting it'll shoot wind signals your way based on what's happening in whatever you're playing.

As you can see in the above image, the device would feature built-in air vents on the inside of the collar, and according to the patent filing, would blow air against the user from different directions, again, based on signals from the control unit. What that sounds like to me is, in a horror game for example, you might feel air brushing up the back of your neck when an enemy is creeping up behind you.

The absurdity of everything aside, this sounds like it could be genuinely immersive if implemented well, even outside horror applications where its usefulness is most obvious. Imagine being able to feel the breeze against your face while driving a car or gliding down from a mountain, or the whoosh of a sword swinging too close to your face.

Again, developers would have to be very considerate when figuring out how to implement this third sense into their games, so its success would depend massively on whether anyone cares enough to make good use out of it. Otherwise, I could see it quickly becoming the world's ugliest and most expensive choker, or worse yet, a gag gift most commonly found in clearance bins and given to unwitting recipients during Krampus Christmas parties where everyone purposefully gives bad presents.

#4071. Guide: Pokémon Pokopia Apples to Applin Event Guide, From Syrupy Apples To A Kitchen Table

Cor! Five new Grass- and Dragon-types for a limited-time only

The Apples to Applin event runs from 16th November to 1st December, 2026, adding five Gen 8 Pokémon to Pokémon Pokopia.

If you've played previous limited-time events, you'll know what to expect. A new Pokémon, Applin, will drop outside the Pokémon Center, asking you to find a currency (Syrupy Apples) in exchange for new items, helping you construct several brand new habitats.

This Pokémon Pokopia guide explains how to start the Apples to Applin event, how to get Syrupy Apples, and everything you need to find Applin evolutions Flapple, Appleun, Dipplin and Hydrapple.

On this page: Pokémon Pokopia Apples to Applin Event Guide, From Syrupy Apples To A Kitchen Table

Before you start, you need to have rebuilt a Pokémon Center. Once done, make sure you have the latest update, and are playing between the dates of 16th November to 1st December, 2026.

As with recent live-events in the second half of the year, you couldn't time travel to this event ahead of time. But once the start date has passed and once you've connected the game to the internet to authenticate the date, you are able to time travel back if you missed it.

Either way, when you log in during the above dates, Applin will appear outside of the Withering Wastes Pokémon Center and ask for you Syrupy Apples. Once you have enough, you can then trade them for event-specific items inside a Pokémon Center, and build three unique habitats.

To get Syrupy Apples, you must visit Dream Islands with the help of Drifloon by interacting with a doll.

Once in a Dream Island, look for apples growing on trees; give them a headbutt and collect your spoils.

You'll find around 40-50 per visit, meaning you'll need to visit on another day to get 80, which is enough to buy one of every event item (or if you're simply unlocking the event habitats, then you just need 70).

Alternatively, can grow your own Syrupy Apple Tree by buying Syrupy Apple Seeds during the event - one of which is a requirement for one of the habitats - if you so choose, allowing you to source Syrupy Apples in a location of your choosing.

When you have some Syrupy Apples, you can head to the Pokémon Center and exchange them at the counter for event-specific items. These are:

The Apples to Applin event has three habitats to unlock:

This means you need to acquire a total of 70 Syrupy Apples to get items for three Habitats.

Unlike past events, this isn't a simple case of buying and combining the items, as the Abundant Apples and Apple Kitchen requires some additional prep and / or other items first.

For Abundant Apples's Syrupy Apple Tree, plant a Syrupy Apple Seed tree in soil prepared with the Rototiller, then water it each day until it grows and sprouts fruit, turning it into a Syrupy Apple Tree.

This will take around three to four days in total, though you can always change the time to do this quicker, and is definitely not what we did to speed up the process.

As for Apple Kitchen's Kitchen Table, if you don't have one already, you can find one of these in the building on the edge of the water west of the Pokémon Center in Bleak Beach (see the mini-map in the below screenshot for the exact location). From there, you can use a 3D Printer to copy a couple more.

Best of luck getting all three habitats before the event wraps!

Guide Pokémon Pokopia: Walkthrough, Unlocks, Tips & Tricks

This isn't the first Pokémon Pokopia event we've covered. And if meeting Applin and their many evolutions has inspired you to keep playing, our Pokémon Pokopia walkthrough leads the way to many more guides that can help.

#4070. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4069. PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio

PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.

The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop.

Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs.

#4067. The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Is Nintendo's Fastest-Selling Switch 2 Game Ever

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo's second remake of the original N64 game that first launched way back in 1998, is the fastest-selling Nintendo-published game on the Switch 2 ever. That accolade comes after the game sold more than 5.2 million copies in just four days following its November 5 launch last week.

This remake is already the Switch 2's second-best-selling Nintendo game at 5.2 million units sold, behind Mario Kart World's impressive 16.48 million copies sold to date. If The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time keeps this pace up, it could one day overtake Mario Kart World, though the Mario Kart series typically holds onto that top spot. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is still far and away the best-selling game on Switch.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the crown jewel of Nintendo's 40th Zelda series anniversary celebration, which also includes other games, products, and even an upcoming worldwide orchestral tour. Plus, a live-action Legend of Zelda film will debut in theaters worldwide on April 30, 2027.

Game Informer gave The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a 9.25 out of 10 in its review, with our reviewer Kyle Hilliard writing, "For many like me, the original Ocarina of Time is an impactful adventure that arrived at a time in their lives when magic still felt real. Playing the game 28 years later and appreciating the care taken to maintain and improve the original vision was the ultimate surprise of the whole experience: I didn't expect to be so moved."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched last week exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

#4066. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

Earlier this month, rumors surfaced about a potential Magic: The Gathering x Dune Secret Lair Superdrop. The rumors quickly spread like wildfire across internet forums like Reddit, but nothing came directly from Wizards of the Coast.

That was until now, when the official Secret Lair Twitter account teased the crossover, revealing it's set to drop in less than two weeks' time.

"The thumper is set and Shai-Hulud is on the move," Wizards of the Coast teased on social media, with a short video of a thumper pounding the sand, followed by the Secret Lair logo. "My Arrakis, My Superdrop goes on sale November 30. #DuneMovie"

This MTG Secret Lair tweet all but confirmed that everything in the recent leak was true. The name, "My Arrakis, My Superdrop," matches the one that was leaked, so we can probably assume everything else was correct.

It said there would be three individual drops based around Sandworms, artifacts, and enchantments, followed by a set of legendary creatures based on eight characters from the Dune movies. The set is reported to include reprints like Sandstorm Convergence and Darksteel Forge, but 11 of the 20 leaked cards are completely new to the Secret Lair drop.

Further details have been confirmed on Reddit, with one of the drops coming in Halo Foil. The commander cards will include some fan-favorite characters, including Paul Atreides, Baron Vladimir Harkonnen, and Chani. The third set, Spice Harvest, is the only one whose price has leaked so far, retailing for $ 59.99.

The Secret Lair Superdrop arrives just in time for the Dune: Part Three movie, set to release in theatres worldwide on December 18, the same day as Avengers: Doomsday. It will be the 13th Secret Lair Superdrop of the year, following the likes of The Hobbit, Lofi Girl, My Little Pony, and Star Trek.

We'll have more coverage of this drop coming soon to TheGamer, including a handy guide, so keep your eyes peeled.

#4064. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4062. Marvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Reportedly Still In Development Amid Rumors Of Its Cancellation

Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

However, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no announced platforms.

Although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

Fan translations have absolutely exploded in the past few years, but with the rise of generative AI in this sort of project, it's gotten downright exhausting trying to keep track of which ones are actually worth your time. But there are still devs putting in old-fashioned elbow grease to make sure even the most obscure of Japan-only curiosities is made playable by a wider audience. Such is the case with Meremanoid, a PS1 JRPG that's now playable in English for the first time.

Meremanoid, originally released in 1999, is a turn-based RPG not entirely dissimilar to something like Final Fantasy VII, albeit at what was surely a dramatically lower budget. Based on an anime that had finished airing a year earlier, it's set entirely underwater, with a world full of mermaids.

Is it good? Well, look – once you start digging deep enough into the PS1 library, you stop asking that kind of question. Instead, the real question is 'Is it interesting?' and it's certainly got enough unique flavor to have entranced the team of hackers and translators who have created the new English patch.

"To me personally, these obscure games are fascinating, and the PS1 library is a veritable treasure trove of them," Chapu, who hacked the game, says in a Reddit post. "I feel anything were there's a language barrier merits a translation. You can probably play, say, a racing or fighting game in Japanese and still enjoy it without understanding the text, but if there's a story involved, that's when I give it a shot!"

The patch is available via Romhack Plaza, and here's arguably the most important bit: "From translation to graphics to coding, this fan translation project proudly features zero use of AI," the devs say in a social media announcement. Seeing devs take on the challenge of translating this kind of obscurity by hand for sheer love of the game still does my heart good.

They might be a little better known than Meremanoid, but our list of the best JRPGs you can play today has all the essentials.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.

#4060. Our first look at Diablo 4's Warlock and the game's next season arrive in today's livestream - watch it here

Diablo 4's latest Developer Update is nearly upon us, and it's one plenty of the game's fans and players have been looking forward to.

Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first announced nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

The Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

The Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

The Developer Update will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

Among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

#4059. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4058. How To Get All Achievements In Dice Hoarder

While you're organizing all those dice, why not collect all the achievements too?

Dice Hoarder is a collectathon game where the goal is to organize a sea of tabletop dice scattered all over the floor of a small shop. The game is simple enough, but it has plenty of achievements to collect that might not be very clear.

Luckily, even though you have to sort through thousands of dice, you only need to earn sixteen achievements over the course of the game. You can claim them all in a single playthrough of the campaign, but you'd have to do it the hard way. Here are all the achievements in Dice Hoarder and how to get them.

In a regular playthrough of Dice Hoarder, you should be able to get every achievement, but one will make it a bit more challenging. Here is a breakdown of all the game's achievements and how to get each one.

Left-click the cat and drag your cursor back and forth to pet it.

Place any die into its slot in the store.

When you find the first floppy disk, install it onto the computer to learn the skill.

Place seven corresponding dice into the correct slot in the store until the slot glows.

After unlocking the resin caster, mix, pour and TKTKT the dice before pulling them out of the slots.

Fill any 50 slots in the store with the correct dice.

Fill any 100 slots in the store with the correct dice.

In any nine-slot display, fill all slots with the correct dice until all slots glow.

Fill a display slot with seven dice, each from a different set.

Take a d20, d12, d10, d8, d6, d4 and percentile die from different sets and put them all in the same slot.

Fill any 200 slots in the store with the correct dice.

Take any d20 in the store and keep tossing it into the rolling tray until you roll a natural 20.

Install every floppy disk on the computer as they show up over the course of the campaign.

Complete the campaign by putting every die in the store in its correct slot

Eat all the hidden edible dice in the shop.

Eat the ten hidden dice throughout the shop that don't have a slot, that are stuck in corners and on shelves.

After unlocking each skill, go into the computer and use XP to level them all up until you reach the max level in each.

Without using True Sight, Dice Summons, Guidance or Critical Sort, finish sorting out all the dice in the store.

There are over 3,000 books to clean up in Librarian: Tidy Up The Arcane Library, and you'll need to put them all away to complete the game.

#4057. Halo: Campaign Evolved Gets Firefight Mode In Free Update This Winter

Halo: Campaign Evolved is getting the fan-favorite Firefight mode via a free update this winter, an Xbox Wire post announces. The update will allow players to team up in cooperative wave-based PvE.

Firefight, which debuted in Halo 3: ODST, lets up to four players team up to survive waves of enemies. The mode has become a popular staple and has appeared in multiple Halo games, but this will be the first time that it has been retroactively added to the original entry.

Xbox FanFest attendees, a global multi-city event, will be the first to go hands-on with Campaign Evolved’s take on Firefight. Additionally, more details about Firefight will be shared during Halo Fest in Seattle on December 12-13, where the mode will also be playable for attendees.

#4056. Review: Mobapad M12 Pro Joy-Con For Switch 2 - The Best Option For Handheld

Mobapad's M12 HD Joy-Con for Switch 2 were exceptional. They are, in many ways, superior to Nintendo’s official offering, largely thanks to the ‘smooth-gliding’ TMR sticks, satisfying mechanical inputs, and comfortable design.

Yet with the absence of mouse controls, I found myself returning to the console’s default Joy-Con 2 until they once again became my go-to options. To be clear, I rarely use mouse mode, but the knowledge that I couldn’t was enough to sway me.

The new M12 Pro Joy-Con eliminate almost every issue I had with their HD predecessors. Available for pre-order at $119.99 (down from the regular price of $149.99), they include every feature from the official Joy-Con 2 – yes, everything. So you’ve got NFC support, 9-axis gyro, mouse controls, a proper ‘C’ button, and HD rumble that feels just as good as the real deal.

Add in the TMR sticks, a proper D-pad, and remappable back buttons, and you’ve got a pair of Joy-Con that, if you can stomach the price, are unquestionably the best option for handheld play.

Since I’ve already reviewed the M12 HD, I’ll focus primarily on the new features in the Pro.

Review Mobapad M12-HD Controllers For Switch 2 - A Clear Step Above Nintendo's Joy-Con 2

To start, the Joy-Con use Switch 2 protocol for connection, meaning the console recognises them as official Switch 2 accessories. This allows for instant connection, no faffing around with pairing settings, and of course, wake-up support with a simple click of the Home button.

Utilising the Switch 2 protocol also ensures that NFC support is always active and not reliant on a Bluetooth toggle, while the Pro now also sports a dedicated ‘C’ button – the HD’s use of a macro to navigate to the Chat app was fine, but a proper button is much better.

Finally, the little on-screen animation when you snap the Joy-Cons in place actually matches the new colour scheme (purple and green), so that’s a lovely little touch.

Mouse mode is perhaps the biggest surprise. I wasn’t expecting any third-party Joy-Con to include this for a while, but to see Mobapad pull it off so well is awesome. Like the official Joy-Con, you can use mouse controls on multiple surfaces, including a pair of jeans, and it remains accurate with minimal lag. What’s more, the ergonomic shape of the M12 Pro means that mouse mode actually feels reasonably comfortable for a change.

Using the face buttons and analogue stick at the same time still feels a tad awkward, but I actually feel like I can grip the Joy-Con properly while moving it across a surface. I can’t say the same for the official Joy-Con 2.

Rumble has also been upgraded. Officially dubbed ‘HD Rumble 2.0’, you can adjust the intensity via controller shortcuts, and it feels incredible. I don’t know if it’s exactly on par with the official Pro Controller, but it’s pretty damn close. In fact, you’ve probably seen videos of the Pro Controller’s rumble matching the tone of the ocarina in Zelda: Ocarina of Time. It’s remarkable stuff, and the M12 Pro does the exact same thing.

In terms of features, those are your main upgrades over the M12 HD. The design, however, has also been slightly changed. In terms of colour, you now have a gradient going from black to purple, and it looks really nice in person. I am, however, conscious that this won’t be to everybody’s taste, so I’m hopeful that Mobapad provides some expanded options in the future.

The darker colour scheme also ensures that, like the HD, the Pro accumulates a few marks over time from fingerprints. It’s not quite so noticeable on the upper purple sections, but you might want to give them a little wipe-down from time to time. Again, some lighter colour options will help to mitigate this.

The last change to highlight is the light-up Mobapad logo located at the bottom of both Joy-Con. I didn’t mind this on the HD, but the logo has been shrunk down drastically on the Pro, opting instead to feature a cool pattern that shimmers with the RGB lighting. It’s a lot more attractive, and looking back on the HD’s logo reveals just how garish it really is. If you’re not keen, however, you can disable the RGB functionality entirely via the Mobapad app.

Mobapad’s M12 HD was already a compelling alternative to Nintendo’s official Joy-Con 2, but its lack of mouse support meant that it failed to become my default option. Now, with the M12 Pro sporting every feature from the Joy-Con 2, including mouse controls and improved HD rumble, I genuinely can’t imagine using anything else.

If you’re someone who enjoys playing the Switch 2 in handheld mode but finds the official Joy-Con lacking in comfort, the M12 Pro will prove a sound investment. It doesn’t get much better than this.

The sample used in this review was provided by Mobapad.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake only just released on November 5, but it's already become the best-selling physical release of the year in the US, a record that'll surely hold against another highly anticipated game releasing in a few days that rhymes with Grand Theft Gelato.

Per Circana's Mat Piscatella, citing sales data through November 7, Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the first physical launch to surpass 1 million units sold in the US since Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom from 2023, further cementing the new remake as an undeniable commercial success, in case there was any doubt. And yet, with GTA 6 looming on the horizon, Ocarina of Time's days as the year's best-selling physical release are likely numbered.

Now, you could make the valid argument that GTA 6 technically isn't getting a physical version considering it's a code-in-box situation where you receive a physical game case but have to download the actual file by typing in a code. In essence, a digital game code inside of a physical case for collectors. That said, Piscatella confirmed in a follow-up post on Bluesky that Circana counts a code in a box as a physical sale, so GTA 6 will definitely qualify at least according to Circana's methods.

After just one week in market, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is 2026's best-selling physical video game in the US. It is the 1st title to surpass 1M physical units in a US launch week since 2023's The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. Source: Circana Retail Tracking Service

It's not a huge surprise to see the Ocarina of Time remake selling so many physical cartridges considering its strong nostalgia appeal, not to mention excellent reviews calling this one of the best remakes of this generation. Our own 5/5-star review calls it  "a remake for the ages, blending the charm and whimsy of the original with more digestible gameplay and stunning visuals."

As GamesRadar+'s Anna Koselke writes, "It's as timeless as it ever was, managing to recreate one of the most beautiful games to date without compromising the magic of its 1998 predecessor – only adding to it. Between newly voiced dialogue, revamped dungeons, fresh puzzles, and more, Hyrule has never felt so alive."

#4054. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4052. What All Floppy Disks Do In Dice Hoarder

Those mysterious floppy disks are pretty useful when you use them to the fullest.

One of the main features of Dice Hoarder is that skills level up through the floppy disks you can find throughout the shop. It adds a bit of mystery once you start getting emails about their enigmatic appearance and what they could mean, but that doesn't make them any less useful.

However, when you pick them up, it helps to know what each one does. Some are self-explanatory, while others might not be clear from the name alone. Regardless, they make your job significantly easier, especially once you level them up. Here are all the floppy disk abilities in Dice Hoarder and how to use them.

As you make your way through the shop and start clearing up some of the dice, you'll find floppy disks lying around in places you might've just looked and not seen anything. When you pick them up, you can identify them only by their color and title.

However, when you install them on the computer, you'll find two types of disks: magical and non-magical. The non-magical ones affect your personal abilities or have some... messages on them, while the magical ones make sorting through the dice a breeze.

There are over 3,000 books to clean up in Librarian: Tidy Up The Arcane Library, and you'll need to put them all away to complete the game.

The non-magical abilities are some of the most useful because they function as quality-of-life updates to your overall character.

Lets you sprint, with consecutive upgrades increasing sprint speed.

Lets you crouch to get lower to the floor and see under tables.

Lets you pick up dice from farther away, with consecutive upgrades increasing that distance.

Lets you place dice into slots from farther away, with consecutive upgrades increasing that distance.

While these are the only non-magical floppy disks that affect your stocking, some floppy disks don't give you abilities but provide story context in the campaign.

You'll have to play through the campaign to properly understand the context of those disks, but as you can imagine, it's not quite as pleasant as the rest of the game.

The magical abilities are what really make stocking the shelves faster and easier. These are the things you couldn't do yourself if you were stocking the shelves of a die shop in real life.

Highlights and draws a line to the correct display for the held die so you don't have to check the computer every time.

Creates a ring around you in which any dice for your held set are highlighted to make them easier to find.

Summons dice from your held set to you from wherever they are in the store. Upgrading it more will summon more dice at a time.

While you're holding a d20, activating this will roll that die, and upon a passed check will complete the set and automatically fill the slot on the display.

These abilities are the best way to organize every die in the store as fast as possible, but be warned. If you want all the achievements, you have to complete the game without using any of these. You can still use the non-magical floppy disks, but the magical ones void the final achievement in the game.

Librarian: Tidy Up The Arcane Library won't tell you where to find the four hidden chest keys, but you'll need them all to unlock Minor Magic!
