#4051. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4050. God Of War Sons Of Sparta Gets PS4 Version And New Content Next Monday

It's been about nine months since Sony Santa Monica and Mega Cat Studios dropped God of War Sons of Sparta as a surprise reveal and launch during a State of Play. If you haven't checked it out yet, the developers are giving you some new reasons to today, unveiling two new modes and a new platform: PlayStation 4.

If you don't remember, God of War Sons of Sparta is a prequel spin-off of the God of War series, showing protagonist Kratos as a 13-year-old soldier, long before his god-killing days. The game features 2D combat and a Metroidvania-style map, along with a fully voiced cast of characters including Scott Menville (who you might recognize as Robin in Teen Titans) as Kratos' brother Deimos, Jack Quaid (who will voice a different character in God of War Laufey next year), and TC Carson, who returns from the original trilogy as the voice of adult Kratos.

Announced in a post on the PlayStation Blog today, Sons of Sparta is making the jump back to Sony's previous console, which is now (brace yourself) 13 years old. Sons of Sparta's 2D pixel art is far less demanding than the other God of War entries, though, so it's no surprise this was possible – it's mainly surprising that they're doing it at all.

For PS5 players who already own the game, developer Mega Cat is also adding two new modes: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode. Hermes Mode, named after the Greek god of wind, mail, and speed, is a speedrun mode that encourages you to beat the game as quickly as possible, complete with a split-based timer in the upper right-hand corner of the screen. Meanwhile, Erebus Mode, named after one of the domains of the underworld (you'll be familiar with it if you've played the Hades games), makes the game far deadlier as Kratos and all his foes die in a single hit. You'll have to wait until you beat the game once to unlock Erebus Mode, but you can access Hermes Mode from a fresh save by entering the following (and semi-familiar) code in the start menu: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad.

The free update and PS4 version will be available next Monday, November 16, at midnight local time. For more Sons of Sparta, check out our review. For more God of War, bad news: God of War Laufey was just delayed until May.

#4049. Dave The Diver's Latest Crossover Update Sees Another Beloved Indie Join The Fray

Since its arrival on Switch a few years back, Dave The Diver has crossed over with just about every other indie game imaginable (a slight exaggeration, but you get our point). Today, developer Mintrocket has announced yet another of these crossovers for its roster, as it is teaming up with Fireshine Games and Pugstorm on some new two-way Core Keeper content.

This crossover update launches on 30th November in both games, with the sandbox survival title gaining some new Blue Hole paraphernalia, and the beloved diving/bar management sim going all mine-y. It's all entirely optional, but it'll be hanging around permanently, so you are free to check it out whenever you fancy.

We'll start with Dave the Diver. As part of the crossover, the game will net a brand-new minigame, where you'll have to pick up a pickaxe and help defend Otto and Sammy's farm from hordes of Core Keeper Cavelings.

You'll be able to dive into the minigame after unlocking the farm through Sammy's VIP event, and there are new charms and figurine rewards for those who play.

The additions aren't quite as grand in Core Keeper, but they're very sweet, nonetheless. Cobra will arrive as a new underground merchant, selling all manner of Dave-themed goodies. There are Momo and Mini Dave pets, a new Bancho-inspired sushi armour, additional furniture items and sound effects, and more.

All of this will arrive in Core Keeper on all platforms on 30th November, while Mintrocket has confirmed that console rollout for the Dave the Diver update might be a little slower (though it will arrive on PC on 30th).

#4048. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

In 2008, Kojima Productions released what was billed as the swan song for Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear series: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots. The game had the staggering task of tying up decades of storytelling by bringing together Solid Snake, Ocelot, Otacon, Raiden, and many more characters for one explosive finale. The adventure centers on a rapidly aging Solid Snake racing against the clock to stop his twin and nemesis, Liquid Snake, one last time. Of course, there are far more bizarre shenanigans at play.

#4046. How To Identify Stolen Items In Probably Stolen

What counts as stolen goods, who brings them in, and how to get away with selling them in Probably Stolen.

You know, for a game labeled Probably Stolen, it's pretty easy to play an entire run without dealing in stolen property at all. But that's no fun; who doesn't want to play the bad guy sometimes? Or at least, the morally grey guy.

If you're interested in dealing with some not-so-legally-acquired goods to make a profit, here's what you need to know and who you need to avoid.

Typically, stolen goods will be things like pharmaceuticals, chemistry products, or sometimes food. All stolen goods will have some level of heat attached to them based on their value in credits. Heat is the game's metric for how obviously stolen they are — higher heat objects will be easily identified as stolen by buyers and Security, while low heat items might be easier to get away with. Heat disapates over time; the longer you have the item in your inventory, the less attention it'll attract. When it hits zero heat, it's no longer considered stolen and can be sold normally.

Stolen goods are also typically sold by a shady customer or, in some cases, wanted criminals. They'll say something to the effect of needing to get rid of their goods quickly, of "finding" them, or similar phrasing. Sometimes the customer will simply be labeled Thief, which does make identifying them much easier, but sometimes you'll be buying from a chemist or pharmacist who's stolen from their workplace.

On day 14 (or day five if you skip the intro), you'll be visited by The Butcher, a wanted Lower Levels criminal who sells meat that's identified as stolen with fairly high heat...don't ask where the meat comes from. He comes back once a week to sell off his goods. You can choose to report him to Security if you want to, but that can have some pretty dire consequences. You can also try shooting him with the shotgun, but this isn't particularly effective. This is, in my opinion, one of the scariest characters in the game.

How to inspect goods, evaluate their worth, and level up your appraisal skills in Probably Stolen.

Storing stolen goods is relatively easy; keep them in a smuggler's bay, which can hold up to a five by five grid of objects. This isn't a ton of room, but you can get an expanded smuggler's bay using the Underground Exchange (you'll need to leave a normal smuggler's bay and eight Oxymore injectors in your trash can overnight), which holds an eight by eight grid of objects.

Put stolen goods into your smuggler's bay immediately upon buying them; don't call up your next customer until they're put away if you can avoid it. My first run of Probably Stolen ended because I got caught with stolen goods on the counter one too many times by Security and got arrested.

Once they're in the smuggler's bay, you can sell off your stolen goods to anyone willing to buy them. Don't try and sell them to Security, for obvious reasons, but most Lower Levels citizens won't care where their product came from as long as you have what they need. ou can hold onto stolen goods until their heat is gone if you want to sell them off normally; again, once they hit a heat of zero, they can safely be removed from the smuggler's bay.

Be careful selling stolen goods; every sale of a good with heat attached to it ups your Possession (Stolen Goods) crime, which can eventually lead to an arrest, which ends your run. To combat this, you can hire Joe Wild's Fixers through his network, who will, for a nightly fee, eliminate these crimes from your record, which can keep you from getting arrested.

Which upgrades should you invest in at the beginning of your next Probably Stolen run for more money or better perks later on?

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4045. "That Was Very Tough" - Indiana Jones Dev Struggled To Transition From Gunplay

Indiana Jones and the Great Circle is one of the biggest surprises in recent years. Developer MachineGames, well known for its ability to make gunning down Nazis immensely satisfying in its Wolfenstein franchise, created what is arguably the best Indy adventure since The Last Crusade.

Yet transitioning from Wolfenstein wasn't exactly easy for the studio. In a new interview with the FRVR podcast (thanks, VGC), design director Jens Andersson explains how the developers found it "very tough" to focus on melee combat, given its expertise in gunplay.

“It was one of those features that we were so afraid of. Especially since MachineGames’ pedigree of Wolfenstein, coming into making Indiana Jones with a team primed to make more gore with heavy weapons, running and gunning… and then ‘oh, we’re going to make a family-friendly adventure’. That was very tough.”

Granted, 'family-friendly' might be a bit of a stretch given the game's 16+ PEGI rating, but we understand the sentiment. To make matters worse, MachineGames had to nail the balance between making guns a last resort for Indy while ensuring they still felt good to use.

“That was non-negotiable because we have a lot of people at Machine that love guns. They love everything about guns. They have people that professionally compete shooting. Gun Nuts. Obviously, you know, from Wolfenstein games that interest has been satiated. And at the game time, you have so many fans of Quake and other shooters out there. So we can’t make gunplay bad, that wouldn’t have been acceptable.”

To ensure that fans of guns still enjoyed the game, MachineGames strived to make melee combat "interesting, fun, and easy". This, combined with making reloading a fairly slow process, encourages you to experiment with your environment and locate more melee weapons.

#4044. The Sims 4 patch makes it so your public lot gatherings won't be interrupted by rogue Sims

Stranger Sims will no longer just crash your public lot events in The Sims 4 to talk about whatever.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

#4043. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 13, 2026

Today is Friday the 13th, but let's not dwell on that. Here are some weekend video games to play. Well, actually, here are some of our biggest stories of the week, and then you can check out some weekend game recommendations.

Also, go ahead and make some space on your Xbox or PlayStation hard drive to make room for GTAVI. It's going to be about 200 GB and you can pre-load it now. Delete those games you're not going to return to. Delete all those video clips you'll never watch from every time you get a Trophy on your PlayStation. And you know what? Go ahead and delete Fortnite, too. It's time.

Calling all sickos of The Rootrees Are Dead, Return of the Obra Dinn, The Incident At Galley House, and everything in between: there’s another good deduction game to obsess over. Funeral for the Sun stars a historian who visits an abandoned Latin American town to piece together its turbulent history, chiefly the truth behind the mysterious disappearance of its hundreds of residents (who were, officially speaking, lost in a fire). Supernatural forces allow players to peer into the town’s past to learn about key people potentially responsible for the calamity, who they must identify by name, establish relationships between, and even match younger and older versions of themselves. You even keep track of information using a multi-function notebook à la The Roottrees Are Dead. Boasting an enticing story, a beautiful painterly art direction, and a tight runtime at roughly 8-hours (or less if you’re really on a roll), Funeral for the Sun is a mystery worth unraveling if you need a new deduction game to cozy up with.

NetEase has continued to impress with the pace and quality of its regular updates to Marvel Rivals, which continues today with the release of an 11th season for the superhero battler. Right here at launch, the notable addition is he arrival of X-Men hero Nightcrawler, who BAMFs his way into battle as a strategist, equally capable of healing allies and taking out foes with his sword and brimstone bombs. As is almost always the case right at a new hero’s launch, it can be hard to snag him on the roster on opening day to see how he plays, but once you do, I expect you’ll find him a versatile healer who can pretty dramatically shake up the battlefield, especially with his Ultimate, which basically consolidates allies and enemies together in one central clump for a frenzied exchange of blows. Alongside the new batch of seasonal cosmetics and events to dive into, it’s once again a good time to don your hero outfit and take on some matches.

Pikmin 4 released on Switch 2 this week (or upgraded to Switch 2 depending on how you look at it), and that's a good thing. Pikmin 4 is the best game in the series and the Switch 2 version is the best version. That's great for those who never finished the game (your save does transfer) or skipped Pikmin 4 when it released in 2023, but if you're looking for an excuse to return to the game and play new content, the Dandori Academy addition is underwhelming. You can read my full thoughts here.

Metaphor: ReFantazio, originally released in 2024, is a great RPG from the creators of Persona. And the Persona lineage is obvious throughout the full game. You have to pick and choose where and with whom you should be spending your time, all while a big world-saving RPG with a memorable party of characters plays out in the foreground.

It released this week for Switch 2 and it’s a game that I think would play well on a handheld device. It’s also just a good RPG to play if you missed it previously.

Fun fact: Metaphor: ReFantazio was the game we had lined up to be the next cover when we were temporarily shut down in in 2024. We went to the studio and had a cover drawn up and everything. You can read the full details of the cover story that never was right here.

You can also read Game Informer's review of Metaphor: ReFantazio by following the link.

As we enjoy the final week in a pre-GTA VI world, what better way to gird your loins for next week’s release, so to speak, than by revisiting the last adventures set in Rockstar’s take on Miami? 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a certified classic that, if you’ve never played it, offers nice foundational insight into what Vice City was like in the ’80s (spoiler: it was a lot like Scarface and Miami Vice). Best of all, Vice City is easily available on current platforms with modernized improvements to boot.

If you want to go even further back, chronologically speaking, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a prequel set two years before the events of Vice City. Maybe, in some extremely minute way, Vice City Stories lays narrative groundwork for GTA VI. It’s unlikely, but you never know. Originally released for PSP in 2006, Vice City Stories is trickier to play if you don’t own Sony's retired handheld or a PlayStation 2, which it was ported to in 2007. But if you can find the means, there’s no better time to check out this often overlooked chapter of Vice City’s history.

I usually hold off on early access games, to preserve my experience for the finished product, but I just couldn’t resist Slay the Spire 2. The co-op gameplay is an awesome, major change, but even just adding a couple of new characters and cards would have satisfied my cravings. To that end, this week’s free update adds a brand new character, the Fool, who I’m eager to test out.

FYI, this new character is only available on the game’s beta, so you’ll have to go into the game settings on steam, click Properties, then Game Versions & Betas, and then opt into the “public-beta” version of the game to check the new content out. The patch notes for this update specifically say, “We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch,” so expect frequent tweaks and a bit of a wait before the Fool joins the main Early Access branch. The new beta update also adds two more game modes: Dread and Blitz, which drastically alter your runs. If you want to wait a little while, the team at Mega Crit will refine these options into a more final form. But if you’re like me, more Slay the Spire 2 is more Slay the Spire 2, and I’m hopping in as soon as I can.

Monster Train 2 was one of my favorite games of last year, so I’m always glad to have a reason to jump back in. This week’s DLC, The Punished, is a perfect opportunity to do so, adding a new clan to the base game’s already packed roster. Since any clan can be combined with a second one to start a run, adding just one more option at the game’s start has an exponential effect, expanding the ways you can approach each attempt. As the DLC’s name implies, the new Punished clan gains buffs when taking damage, and you get new suite of cards that damages the whole playing field at once, harming foes and bolstering your allies. Even if you’re not checking out the DLC, the base game is absolutely worth picking up – just read my glowing review.

If you’ve been hankering for a new direction to go with your tabletop RPG group, may I recommend the incredibly versatile Cypher System from Monte Cook Games? The new Character Rulebook includes everything you need to get started, and set your adventures in virtually any fictional backdrop you can imagine, from hard sci-fi to gritty horror to high fantasy. Cypher’s polished approach to narrative-first and player-focused game sessions is much easier to pick up than many new rules systems, but it has enormous flexibility to deliver smart, creative, and exciting adventures that can help to change things up if your playing group has been in a rut.

It was in the works long before Jonathan Majors' firing

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Kevin Feige has revealed that the pivot to Avengers: Doomsday from The Kang Dynasty was not as surprising as it first seemed. The Marvel head explained that they were always considering bringing Doctor Doom in "midway" during the movie.

Speaking to Empire magazine, he said (H/T The Playlist): "It probably would still have been called The Kang Dynasty, but it would have been a set-up for Doom, midway through that movie," adding that they first approached Robert Downey Jr's agent at the Ant-Man And The Wasp: Quantumania premiere.

Feige went on to confirm that the situation around Jonathan Majors' exit from Marvel was "delicate". The actor was dropped by Marvel after he was found guilty of assault in December 2023. "We didn't want to rush into any rash decisions in terms of employment. People think there was a cause-and-effect with Jonathan's issues, and that certainly accelerated some things. But the Doom of it all was well underway before that."

Avengers: Doomsday sees Downey Jr. return to the MCU in a new role, becoming the biggest villain that the heroes have faced yet. In order to defeat him, three different universes (the OG MCU, the Fantastic Four, and the Fox X-Men universe) are all teaming up. However, in the meantime, it seems like Doom has been assembling his own team composed of the Hulk and Scarlet Witch…

One thing we do know is that Doom is not a Tony Stark variant in the new movie. Not sure yet what that means about their shared resemblance, but in Feige we trust…

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in UK cinemas on December 16 and US theaters on December 18. Check out all the other upcoming Marvel movies and shows you need to know about.

#4040. Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

Finally, a PC specification list that actually indicates resolution and framerate targets, and doesn't leave console players behind.

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

#4038. Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (November 14-15)

It's the penultimate weekend to get stuck into the games you'd like to finish before November 19th rolls up.

It's WAYP time, people! You know the score by now, so let's hear what you're playing this weekend! This is your opportunity to have a chat with one another about what's good, what's worth playing, why you're vibing, or maybe, not vibing with certain games. It's an open floor, PX'ers.

Alrighty then, let's get into it. Here's what we're playing on Xbox this weekend:

Recently, I haven't been trying to complete anything, grind online, or chase a Mythic cheevo. I'm just vibing with my Xbox. Honestly, I think GTA 6 has me in a bit of a chokehold, keeping me from starting anything I might not finish. With that in mind, Hozy has been the perfect lil' game to sit down and chill with on a rainy day.

Lots of games are getting little bits of my attention, including Silver Pines, TCG Card Shop Simulator, and Gears of War: E-Day, to name a few. But, my main game at the moment is It Takes Two. I've absolutely loved playing it with my wife. The best bit is how into it she is, that and the bonded trauma it inflicts!

Something I'd like to get back into is Marathon. That new Symbiosis trailer looked awesome, and I'm hoping to lock-in and get that Mythic. I think all I need is to grind to level 100 and it'll be mine. Shouldn't be too much of a time commitment, right?

But I'll be real. I'm playing a lot of Zelda: Ocarina of Time right now. It's a perfect remake of a childhood favourite, and it's feeding my inner kid. He's a happy boy.

GTA 6 is right around the corner, and you better believe it's going to take up the rest of the year in terms of dominating my free time. That means it's not really wise to get stuck into anything too meaty right now, although I'm keen to check out Shrek 2 Remastered and see whether Aspyr's new port does the OG Xbox title justice or not.

I might even play a bit of GTA: Chinatown Wars on my 3DS. I finally started playing that game about a year ago, and even though it's rough around the edges by today's standards, I'm enjoying how unique it is compared to other entries.

#4037. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

#4036. Cleanser Man Is Mega Man: Dual Override’s Boss Design Contest Winner

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:

Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” says game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC.  To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

#4035. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4034. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

#4033. Shigeru Miyamoto To Receive The Inaugural 'Legend Award' At The 30th D.I.C.E. Awards

Award will be presented only once per decade

The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS) has announced that Shigeru Miyamoto, the creator of iconic Nintendo franchises like Super Mario and The Legend of Zelda, will receive the inaugural Legend Award at the upcoming 30th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards ceremony on Thursday, 18th February 2027.

The award, which will only be presented once per decade, 'recognises an industry icon whose enduring vision continues to redefine interactive entertainment'. It's designed to honour creators whose achievements have already earning lasting universal acclaim, while celebrating their 'immeasurable impact and influence'.

Meggan Scavio, President of the AIAS, said the following:

“Shigeru Miyamoto is widely recognized as one of the most respected and impactful figures in the games industry and beyond. We believe he perfectly embodies our inaugural Legend Award through his impact and reach, and we are so humbled and excited to have Mr. Miyamoto accept this award at the 30th anniversary of the D.I.C.E. Awards."

Though his current focus is on the production of movies and theme parks, Miyamoto-san is arguably the most recognisable figure in Nintendo's history, and it's difficult to imagine whether the company would even exist today without his creations.

He most recently appeared during a Pikmin Day Direct presentation, during which he revealed a new demo for Pikmin 4 on Switch 2 along with some Pikmin Bloom updates and the commencement of monthly Hello! Pikmin movies on the Nintendo Today app.

#4032. 2027 Video Game Grammy Nominations Include Avatar: Frontiers Of Pandora For The Third Time

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

James Bond writers Robert Wade and Neil Purvis have weighed in with their thoughts on Robert Pattinson's casting as 007. The writers, who penned the franchise from The World Is Not Enough to No Time to Die, are big fans of the move.

Speaking to Deadline, they called Pattinson "a terrific choice, very exciting." They said that Daniel Craig "is a hard act to follow in terms of chops" but that "Robert has what it takes to – we liked the sly wit he brought to the spy in Tenet, and with this decision it's clear Denis [Villeneuve] wants to keep Bond cool."

The news that Pattinson is taking over the role came after weeks of speculation about the actors who had been screen-testing. Among the candidates were Josh O'Connor, Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, and Nicholas Hoult, who all reportedly made it to the final stages.

Pattinson won out, and according to Bond 26 director Villeneuve, he "has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new". In a statement, he also said: "Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007."

We've already had a first look at Pattinson's Bond in the suit, but it will be a while before he orders a martini on our screens. Bond 26 is being written by Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight and is expected to be released in 2028.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

#4027. Make Room For GTAVI By Deleting Your PS5 Trophy Clips

Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.

You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.

Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.

First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button.

Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips.

After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again.

In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.

#4026. Five Games Are Confirmed For Xbox Game Pass In December 2026 So Far

We've made a habit of casting our gaze ahead and sharing with you an early look at what's in store for December 2026's Xbox Game Pass lineup. So far, we know of five games scheduled to arrive in a few weeks' time.

Our highlight of the bunch is probably A Game About Digging A Hole Together. On the surface it might not seem like the biggest game, but the more you dig down, the better. At least that was the case with the single-player version of the game. This one is co-op!

It's worth mentioning that Dumpster Gang is indeed coming to Xbox Series consoles in March, but will be launching onto PC Game Pass December 3. Then of course, expect to see plenty more games added to December's offering over the coming weeks.

So, without any further ado, here's what's confirmed for Xbox Game Pass in December 2026 so far:

On this page: Five Games Are Confirmed For Xbox Game Pass In December 2026 So Far

See the world through the eyes of a brave little mouse in this enchanting 3D co-op adventure. Explore breathtaking landscapes inspired by Northern Sweden, solve puzzles, and be a force for good in a land where heartwarming storytelling and the beauty of nature intertwine.

Play as a gang of mischievous raccoons in this chaotic co-op sandbox for 1-4 players. Complete ridiculous missions, steal everything you can carry, and outsmart a relentless Exterminator determined to throw your gang behind bars.

Freestyle Football 2 is a fast-paced, 5v5 match-based online multiplayer soccer game. Each position has a unique role, and you'll utilize a variety of strategies and skills to achieve victory with your team. Stylish play and unique characters transform the pitch into a stage.

The latest main branch update doesn't include The Fool or the new game modes

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Slay the Spire 2's latest character, The Fool, is so overpowered that it's only a matter of time before they're hit with the nerf hammer – a point that developer Mega Crit seems to be alluding to as it notes that the latest content to hit the roguelike's beta branch is going to need "quite a bit" of polishing before it comes to the game's main branch.

Mega Crit says as much in the patch notes for Slay the Spire 2's third major main branch update, which rolled out a few hours ago, "bringing all of the content, art, balance changes, and bug fixes from v0.108.0-v0.111.0" that beta branch players have been getting stuck into already. This notably doesn't include v0.113.0 – last week's beta patch that introduced two new game modes and The Fool in the roguelike's biggest update yet.

There's a reason for that, though. "While the new character and game modes on the current beta branch are the talk of the town right now, all that stuff will need to be tested and polished up quite a bit more before it reaches the main branch," Mega Crit explains today.

If you've tried out The Fool at all yet, this, uh, isn't surprising. As our senior writer and resident Slay the Spire 2 expert Austin Wood so eloquently puts it, they're "balanced like a barbell with six plates on one end and two on the other."

To be fair, Mega Crit already hinted that nerfs were planned from the moment The Fool was introduced, saying: "We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch." Have fun with them while it lasts, basically.

Back to today, Mega Crit notes that "we're not sure when" The Fool and those aforementioned game modes will be ready for the main branch, encouraging anyone interested to switch over to the beta to give them a go.

Slay the Spire 2 devs declare the "perfect card," and of course it's one I thought was bad.

#4024. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

#4023. Rumour: Atlus May Be Gearing Up For A Huge Persona 6 Reveal

After what felt like an age waiting for the Persona franchise to make its Switch debut, Sega and Atlus are now all-in on the Switch 2. Persona 4 Revival is scheduled to launch on 20th May 2027, while Persona 6 has also been confirmed for the hybrid console.

Atlus is in full marketing mode for Persona 4 Revival, but our pals over at Push Square have reason to believe that the company may be gearing up to properly reveal Persona 6 in the coming weeks.

This comes from Reddit user ronakwya, who notes that Atlus recently updated the official website for Persona 6. Apparently, however, this was the kind of update that allows Atlus to perform significant changes to the website in preparation for a big public reveal.

Ronakwya has also pointed to the gameplay reveal of Persona 4 Revival as a potential hint. Its own website was also updated in a similar manner roughly one month prior to its big reveal at the Xbox Games Showcase in June 2026.

So, which big gaming event is taking place in just less than a month from now..? Yep, The Game Awards 2026.

This all seems incredibly convenient though, and to be honest we're a little sceptical. As pointed out by Push Square, it would make little sense for Atlus to pull attention away from Persona 4 Revival at this stage to host a full reveal for Persona 6.

In our opinion, we could definitely see a similar reveal during the Xbox Games Showcase in 2027 after the release of Revival in May (February for other platforms). We're happy to be wrong, as we're proper itching to see some gameplay from the next mainline entry, but we're not holding our breath.

#4022. Star Wars: Galactic Racer Gets Local Splitscreen Multiplayer Next Year

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been one of 2026’s breakout titles, but much of the game’s praise stems from its exceptional roguelike single-player mode. If you want to race against human players, you can only do so online. Thankfully, for fans of couch multiplayer, that’s going to change.

Developer Fuse Games announced yesterday that local splitscreen multiplayer is coming to Star Wars: Galactic Racer early next year. The mode lets you race up to three other players on the same screen. That's pretty much all there is to it, but given that local multiplayer was the game's biggest omission and, as a result, the most requested addition, there's probably no better news for Galactic Racer fans.

We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to develop a new mode: Free Play. Choose your vehicle, character, planet, and track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local splitscreen action.[image or embed]

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC. Read our review of the game here.

#4021. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4020. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#4019. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Just Got A Free 1.2 Update, Adding New Game Plus

The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the year's biggest, most ambitious games, and the developers over at Rebel Wolves have done a good job cleaning up bugs and performance issues in the weeks since launch. Today, that trend continued; the new 1.2 update is out now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and it adds New Game Plus.

The new mode is uniquely ideal for a game like Dawnwalker. The narrative is very player-driven, whether it has to do with your literal dialogue options, your ability to manage your vampiric hunger, or the order you complete quests, and all of these elements can cause your experience to vary wildly. It makes sense, then, that players would want to jump back in to try things again and see what might happen if the game is played differently, and New Game Plus allows them to do that while keeping combat fresh.

According to the update notes on the Dawnwalker website, "NG+ unlocks after you complete the game’s Epilogue and lets you experience the story again while keeping your progress – mainly your character level, skills, and inventory." You don't gain access to these skills until you complete the prologue, however, which marks the adventure's proper start.

The new mode will also rebalance the world's level scaling. In the base game, certain areas are much harder than others, but in New Game Plus, all enemies will rise in power to match your level, meaning you can explore the world in whatever order you want. On that note, the level cap has also been raised to 100, and protagonist Coen can collect new, more powerful versions of weapons marked with an "NG+" label.

That's basically everything in this update. Rebel Wolves also added some slight tweaks to combat in the base game and adjusted some geometry in the open world, but the main focus here was New Game Plus. This is in contrast to the 1.1 update, which added a much wider suite of bug fixes and made the game run more smoothly.

#4017. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

#4016. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Crowned 2026's "Best-Selling Physical Video Game In The US"

The Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 got off to an outstanding start, selling over five million copies (approx 5.2 million units) in just four days. Sales in the UK and Japan have contributed to this, and now, Circana Retail Tracking Service has shared data about the title's US launch.

As highlighted by Circana's senior director and video game industry advisor Mat Piscatella (via social media), "after just one week", Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is this year's "best-selling physical video game in the US". Interestingly, it's the first title to surpass one million physical units in a US launch week since the 2023 Switch title, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Considering the year is almost over, and Grand Theft Auto 6's retail release is actually a "code-in-box", we imagine Ocarina's remake will hold onto the title of 2026's best-selling physical game (that's actually a proper physical game). However, there is one technicality - Circana tracks and reports "code-in-box" sales as "new physical video game sales", so Zelda may not actually keep the crown. And GTA 6 has already smashed pre-order records.

According to Nintendo's official data, Ocarina of Time is currently the second-highest selling Switch 2 game globally. As we previously noted, this puts it ahead of Donkey Kong Bananza's lifetime sales of 5.05 million, and the Switch 2 launch title Mario Kart World leads with 16.48 million sales. So it's still a tremendous effort for the remake of the legendary N64 title.

In our review here on Nintendo Life, we awarded Ocarina of Time's Switch 2 remake 9/10 stars, calling it the "best way to play one of the most seminal games of all time". After a brief dip to 95, it's once again sitting on a Metacritic score of 96/100.

#4014. Spider-Man: Brand New Day extended cut is out just before Avengers: Doomsday with "more surprises"

It's official: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is getting a re-release, complete with new scenes.

Brand New Day – as the initial rumors suggested earlier in November – will return to cinemas on December 4, just two weeks before Avengers: Doomsday.

"Welcome to a brand new Brand New Day," Sony Pictures announced on Twitter. "The record-breaking movie is coming back to the big screen on December 4 with an extended cut featuring new scenes and a couple more surprises."

Those new scenes and surprises are under wraps for the time being, but we would be shocked if Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple wasn't part of the extended cut – especially given how transparent the Ahsoka actor was about being left out of the movie.

The surprises, too, could be Avengers: Doomsday-shaped. The Brand New Day post-credits scene suggests Doom is hunting Spidey, while we already know Hulk was on the supervillain's radar courtesy of Avengers: Endgame Encore's bonus footage.

The re-release is also a chance for Brand New Day to cement its standing as the third highest-grossing movie of all time with $2.5 billion dollars (for a few weeks, at least).

Starring Tom Holland, Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Sadie Sink, and Jon Bernthal, Spider-Man: Brand New Day sees Peter Parker coming to terms with a world that no longer knows he is Spider-Man – all while battling a terrifying threat he can't see. That, of course, would be revealed as Jean Grey, with Sadie Sink later officially named as part of 2028's X-Men movie.

For more on what the MCU has cooking up next, we have a complete guide to upcoming Marvel movies. There's also a look at how to watch the Marvel movies in order for those still thwipping through a pre-Doomsday marathon.

#4013. Eight Classic Games Are Available Today With Xbox Game Pass Essential (November 15)

A series of classic Xbox titles to celebrate the 25th anniversary

Happy 25th anniversary of Xbox day! To celebrate the occasion, we've got eight games joining the Xbox Game Pass Essential tier, mostly from the Xbox 360 era - and all classic games in their own right.

All three Banjo-Kazooie entries are fantastic, of course (even Nuts & Bolts!), while Perfect Dark is an FPS masterpiece of its time, and Viva Pinata just celebrated its 20th anniversary. Halo: Spartan Assault is a fun twin-stick shooter, and Gears of War: Judgment is the perfect next entry if you've just finished Gears of War: E-Day's campaign.

Just to clarify, you've already got access to all of these games if you're part of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate or Xbox Game Pass Premium already, but this marks the first time they've become available to Xbox Game Pass Essential members.

On this page: Eight Classic Games Are Available Today With Xbox Game Pass Essential (November 15)

The bear and bird's first ever outing available in full. Loads of rollicking fun to be had here and with the legendary Stop N Swop feature reinstated. You’ll never look the same again at a jigsaw.

The bear and bird’s second outing available in full. Loads of rollicking fun to be had here and with the legendary Stop N Swap feature reinstated. The best use of a backpack in a game ever!

The heroic bear and bird return at last to defend Spiral Mountain from their nemesis Gruntilda. Groundbreaking vehicular platforming awaits in wild new worlds packed with features and faces old and new. Build awe-inspiring vehicles and tackle the Jiggy challenges in any way you see fit!

In the immediate aftermath of Emergence Day, the fate of the world rests on the shoulders of young COG lieutenant Damon Baird and his team - Kilo Squad. As the world of Sera is destroyed around them, Kilo must rise up, break the rules and take the fight to a horrifying new enemy in this blockbuster prequel to one of the most celebrated franchises in gaming history.

Halo: Spartan Assault is a fast paced top-down shooter set during the timeline between “Halo 3” and “Halo 4,” progress your Spartan career as you engage in over 30 exciting Campaign missions using many of favorite Halo weapons, vehicles and armor abilities.

Experience every twist of the story, every stray bullet, every gadget and upgrade, every newly polished texture – and top it all off with full access to multiplayer modes now playable across the globe through Xbox LIVE.

Attract and tame your favourite Piñatas. There are more than 60 species that roam wild on Piñata Island. Personalise everything from the grass at your feet to the hat on your Piñata's head. Welcome to Piñata Island, enjoy your stay!

Welcome back to Piñata Island where Prof. Pester's latest scheme has lead to disaster. Visit the scorching desert or icy wastes to trap new species. Train them, dress them, then send them to a party! We’ve new Piñatas, new activities, new features and new secrets, so come visit and find out why people never want to leave.
