#4012. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

And, as ever, it’s worth checking if you’re missing any of these Love and Deepspace codes to get some in-game freebies.

#4011. Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off A Third Of Its Staff

Firaxis, the studio behind the Civilization series, has laid off around 60 employees, representing a third of its staff. The report comes from Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier.

In a statement provided to Bloomberg by a spokesperson from 2K, a subsidiary of Firaxis' owner, Take-Two, “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

In addition to the 60 affected staffers, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is also departing. Bloomberg also reports, via anonymous Firaxis employees speaking to the outlet, that the studio is working on an unannounced XCOM game that has had a challenging development, with the team recently missing an important development milestone. This project, if it releases, will be the first Firaxis-developed XCOM game since XCOM: Chimera Squad in 2020.

Firaxis’ most recent release is Civilization VII, which launched in February 2025 to favorable reviews but initially "slow" sales, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick last August.  The game currently has a Mixed reception on Steam after Firaxis spent the last year updating the game to address player complaints. Before Civilization VII, Firaxis shipped Marvel's Midnight Suns in 2022, another critically well-received game that failed to meet sales expectations.

#4010. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

#4009. Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Has Been Updated To Version 1.1.4

Konami has released a new update for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse on the Switch and other platforms this week.

Although it's only a small one, it does include some adjustments and fixes. This includes a slight change to the "effective range" of the "Life Drain" spell. Here's the rundown from Konami's official website about everything included in the Version 1.1.4 update:

The following changes and fixes have been made in this update: - The version number is now displayed at the bottom of the title screen. - Adjusted the effective range of the “Life Drain” spell. - Fixed an issue where the screen could remain black after loading under certain conditions. - Fixed various other issues.

Belmont's Curse is currently available for the Switch. While there's no Switch 2 Edition, if you do play this title on Nintendo's new hardware, you'll get a frame rate boost. And if you haven't tried it out yet, you can download a demo from the eShop.

You can find out more about this new Castlevania entry iun our review here on Nintendo Life. We gave it 8/10 stars, calling it "one of the best Castlevania games in a long time thanks to its combat variety and smart whip integrations".

#4008. YouTubers Share Their Amazing Home Videos From The Most Important Day In Xbox History

Happy birthday, Xbox! It's exactly 25 years today since the original Xbox console launched in North America on November 15th of 2001, and it turns out multiple people captured the moment via some amazing home video footage.

We've talked about one of these videos before — the ridiculously cool one from MyRetroLife, who has become a YouTube star since uploading his footage multiple years ago. His short clip of "booting up an original Xbox on launch day" has a whopping 4.6 million views, while his more elaborate story about it (which you can watch down below) has almost 900,000 views.

We're not affiliated with him, but you should go check out his other stuff as well - it's really entertaining!

It turns out there's more footage on YouTube from November 15th that we weren't aware of though, with this next example coming from The Great Gambino. They have much less of a high-profile following than MyRetroLife, but their three-minute Xbox footage is equally as interesting and nostalgic to watch, so it's well worth a view!

Apparently, this video was somewhat quietly uploaded to their YouTube channel a few years ago, but exploded into the millions of views after other people reposted it to the likes of TikTok, Facebook and other social media platforms.

They uploaded the most complete version of it a couple of years ago, which you can see below:

Of course, some of us Pure Xbox users were also there back on November 15th of 2001, unboxing our original Xbox consoles for the first time, but it's quite special to see the moment captured on camera for us to see in 2026!

There's more official footage of the OG Xbox launch out there as well if you go searching for it, but we reckon it's the home videos that paint a more accurate picture of what it was like to be an Xbox fan at the very beginning.

It's also the kind of thing that makes you realise how old you truly are!

Update: We've just come across another one! Here's an Xbox home video from thedanceman on YouTube:

#4007. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

#4006. Splatoon 3 Version 12.0.0 Out Now, Here Are The Full Patch Notes

The dev team also has another update on the way

Update [Wed 18th Nov 2026, 12am]: This new update for Splatoon 3 (Version 12.0.0) is now officially available to download. You can see the patch notes below.

Original Story: Nintendo's team-based squid-shooter Splatoon 3 is still going strong, and this week the title is getting updated to Version 12.0.0.

This major update will come with changes to multiplayer, including weapon adjustments. There are also changes to Anarchy Battle, X Battles and challenges. Additionally, there are changes to the GameChat feature on Switch 2. Nintendo also notes how its next update after this one will focus on multiplayer game balance.

You can get the full rundown in the official patch notes below (via Nintendo's official support page):

On this page: Splatoon 3 - Version 12.0.0 (17th November 2026)

Sections marked "on Nintendo Switch 2" apply only to Nintendo Switch 2. All other changes apply to both Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch.

Made it possible to participate with a friend in traditional X Battles as a group of two.

Added a feature that allows players to open GameChat and invite friends from their group while playing modes with friends, such as battles or Salmon Run.

This update focuses on making changes to matchmaking and multiplayer balance.

For X Battles, we have added a feature to allow players to play as a pair with a friend. The goal of this feature is to expand the range of ways to play, and we will introduce it on a trial basis starting in Chill Season 2026. After we have introduced it, we will comprehensively analyze how these battles are actually played and how the gameplay situation shifts, including for players who are not playing with a friend. Then we will decide whether to continue providing this feature in future seasons.

For Anarchy Battle (Series), we have changed the matchmaking system such that, in exchange for removing the feature allowing players to continue with the same team, matchmaking will now complete more quickly and with less imbalance of skill level and equipped weapons between players and their opponents.

For Challenges, we have changed how Challenge Power is calculated to make it easier to raise Challenge Power the more wins a player has. With this change, between players who would have ended up with about the same Challenge Power under the previous system, the player who attained the greater number of wins will have the higher final Challenge Power.

For multiplayer balance, we made a variety of changes to main, sub, and special weapons, including changes to the flight distance of Blaster shots.

With most weapons, when a player fires while moving, the player's movement speed is added to the shot's speed to a certain extent, resulting in a more natural trajectory. For Blasters, we have minimized the change in shot flight distance caused by this effect, making it easier to maintain an appropriate distance against an opponent’s Blaster.

Among the special weapons, we have changed the Reefslider because, while there is statistically little impact on victories in matches between extremely skilled players, it has a high impact on matches between less skilled players. The intention behind this change is to alleviate that striking difference. By narrowing the area affected by the explosion we have made it so that players cannot reap the maximum benefit without using it at the precise position. On the other hand, we have extended the invulnerability period to make it harder for opponents who used terrain to survive the explosion to counterattack and easier for the player to make follow-up attacks.

For the Tenta Missiles, we have decreased the vulnerability while firing and expanded the area where it is possible to lock on to opponents. As a result, it will now be easier to use, even in situations where opponents are nearby the player. By decreasing the impact interval, it becomes easier to defeat opponents who are slow to dodge, but the duration for which they must keep dodging is reduced.

We have also added a feature for Nintendo Switch 2 that will make it easier to use GameChat.

The next update will focus on changes to multiplayer balance.

If you haven't already played the game on Switch 2, there's a free upgrade available which includes visual improvements and frame rate optimisations for the platform. In some related news, Splatoon Raiders has also received an eShop demo this week!

#4005. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

Kevin Feige acknowledges Quantumania underperformed, but he still likes Kang

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Marvel boss Kevin Feige has admitted that Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania didn't perform the way he wanted, but he's still happy with Kang.

Kang was played by Jonathan Majors, who was dropped by Marvel after he was found guilty of reckless assault in the third degree and harassment in December 2023. Avengers 5, which is now Avengers: Doomsday and stars Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom, was originally going to be titled The Kang Dynasty.

"Quantumania was not received the way we would have liked," Feige told Empire magazine. "There are many elements of that that we're proud of, the Kang performance being one of them. But we were changing [The Kang Dynasty] even at that point."

In the same interview, Feige further elaborated on plans to replace Kang with Doctor Doom. "We didn't want to rush into any rash decisions in terms of employment. People think there was a cause-and-effect with Jonathan's issues, and that certainly accelerated some things. But the Doom of it all was well underway before that," he explained.

That means The Kang Dynasty wouldn't have been what anyone expected. "It probably would still have been called The Kang Dynasty, but it would have been a set-up for Doom, midway through that movie," Feige revealed.

Doomsday arrives this December 18, with a supersized cast that includes the likes of the Fox X-Men, the Fantastic Four, the Thunderbolts, Chris Hemsworth's Thor, Anthony Mackie's Captain America, and Chris Evans's Steve Rogers.

While you wait, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV shows for everything else that's on the way.

#4003. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#4002. Talking Point: As Xbox Celebrates Its 25th Anniversary, What Are Your Hopes For The Next 25 Years?

Maybe we'll be looking back on this in 2051!

The celebrations for Xbox's official 25th anniversary roll on! We've finally arrived at November 15th, which marks the exact date when the original Xbox launched all the way back in 2001. How time flies!

Of course, this is a great chance to reflect on everything that's happened over the past 25 years, which we've been doing in various articles throughout the month (and indeed the year), but it's also an opportunity to think about the next 25 years and where Xbox as a brand might be headed in the future.

I think the cynical view, and perhaps the logical view, is that Xbox won't exist by the time we get to 2051. Let's not forget that PlayStation was still in its infancy 25 years ago, SEGA had just got out of the console business after being a major player for so long, and Nintendo hadn't even released the GameCube in North America until November 18th of 2001.

Feature 25 Years Later, How Many Of These Original Xbox Launch Titles Have You Played?

From the original North American launch on November 15, 2001

In other words, 25 years is a very long time, and we've seen many ups and downs from Xbox throughout its history. The glory days of Halo, Xbox Live and the Xbox 360 were followed up by a horribly botched Xbox One launch, and the Xbox Series era has been summed up as everything from extremely promising to extremely disappointing, now hovering somewhere in the 'cautiously optimistic' territory for some Xbox fans since Asha Sharma took the helm earlier in 2026.

While console sales might be down, and the Xbox CEO keeps talking about a need to "return to growth", there's every reason to believe Xbox might still be a powerhouse in 25 years' time. Microsoft's backing is obviously a big aspect of that — assuming the brand never gets sold off — but so is the mountain of incredible first-party IP (Minecraft, Call of Duty, World of Warcraft, etc.) that should continue to rake in money over the next decade at least, coupled with the ability to innovate in the hardware space and eventually win back some market share with handhelds and consoles.

Realistically, the answer to all of this is that we don't have an answer - it's impossible to predict a future that's still 25 years out, especially when Xbox's mission statement appears to have changed on an almost yearly basis during the 2020s. There's no doubt that Xbox will face many challenges in the 25 years that are ahead and it'll be forced to adapt and innovate along the way, but I wouldn't be surprised if we're still talking about it in 2051!

For what it's worth, here's what Xbox boss Asha Sharma said on this topic a few days ago:

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically. As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this. [..] A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

"I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays. Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen."

Talking Point As Xbox Celebrates 25 Years, What's Your First Ever Xbox Memory?

News Asha Sharma Issues Statement On Xbox's 25th Anniversary And The Future Of Gaming

#4001. PSA: Splatoon Raiders Demo Splashes Onto The Switch 2 eShop Today

Splatoon Raiders made quite the splash when it arrived on the Switch 2 earlier this year, and if you haven't already had a chance to try it out, there's now a demo.

You can download this demo from the eShop, and it comes loaded with three stages set in the Spirhalite Islands, three preselected loadouts, and reunites you with the crew from Deep Cut.

Of course, this title is somewhat different to the mainline experience. It's more of a story-driven experience, where you work your way through stages and waves of enemies to progress to the next stage and unlock more weapons, upgrades and content. It also offers co-op multiplayer, if you do want to team up with family and friends.

According to Nintendo's latest financial sales data, Splatoon Raiders has now sold 2.42 million copies, placing it in the top-ten best-selling games on the Switch 2. We awarded it an "excellent" 9/10 stars when it arrived in July, noting how it offers one of the most enjoyable gameplay loops on Nintendo's new system.

In some related news today, Splatoon 3 has been updated to Version 12.0.0. It includes changes to multiplayer and much more. You can find out more in our previous story. The last game update for Splatoon Raiders was in August.

#4000. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

Yasunori Mitsuda says let Yuji Horii "create a brand-new RPG" instead

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dragon Quest has pressed on following the death of Dragon Ball icon Akira Toriyama, who served as the 40-year-old RPG series' character and monster designer – but the use of the manga legend's art style after his passing is now proving controversial.

Square Enix recently lifted the veil on a new mobile entry, dubbed "Dragon Quest Quest RPG The Cursed Tree and the Chosen Isle," sparking online discussions about the continued use of Toriyama's aesthetic in Dragon Quest games. From comments on how faithful things look (or don't look) now to the designer's own art to worries that this isn't the correct way to carry on his legacy, it's been… a lot. And it's reaching fellow developers themselves.

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda is one such dev, sharing his thoughts on the controversy in a new blog post (as translated by Automaton). "The Dragon Quest RPG: The Cursed Tree and the Chosen Isle illustrations in Akira Toriyama-san's style have been a hot topic recently," he writes, "but I think this kind of approach isn't good for the artist, or Toriyama-san's fans, or even the late Toriyama-san himself."

According to Mitsuda, Square Enix should wrap up the Dragon Quest series and allow Yuji Horii to start fresh with something entirely new. "Since it's pretty much impossible to create anything truly new no matter how much you try, I feel like it would be best to retire the Dragon Quest series and let Horii-san create a brand-new RPG," he admits, going on to share his love for Dragon Quest – a title that's stood the test of time since 1986.

Its effect on the world, both developers and fans alike, is undeniable – but I get where Mitsuda is coming from. It might finally be time to close the book on Dragon Quest and see what else Horii has to offer, perhaps in an entirely new style that incorporates the genius of other artists. Regardless, I'd say Toriyama's influence will live on in some way or another… It's almost impossible for it not to.

#3998. Blizzard will talk about Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred one last time before the expansion's launch next week

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#3997. Rumour: Persona 6 Blowout Primed for The Game Awards

There's reason to believe that we'll get our first proper look Persona 6 next month, during The Game Awards.

This rumour stems from Reddit user ronakwya, who has, rather diligently, been keeping tabs on the game's Japanese website. The idea being that if the domain receives any backend updates, it could mean that an announcement is incoming.

And guess what? The site was altered just recently, on the 8th November — and it wasn't just some standard update. This was, apparently, the kind of renewal that happens when a company overhauls a domain — as in, the website is redesigned to fall in line with a big announcement, ready to be made public when the bomb drops.

But what really adds a lot of weight to this discovery is that Atlus followed this pattern almost exactly with Persona 4 Revival, before its own reveal earlier this year. Revival's teaser website received a behind-the-scenes overhaul roughly one month before appearing at the Xbox Games Showcase in the summer.

The Game Awards is obviously happening one month from this update — on the 10th December — and so you can certainly argue that things are starting to add up.

News Persona 6 Could Get Its Big Reveal in March, as Atlus Announces First Super Live Show in Four Years

Rumour Persona 6 Release Is Way Closer Than Most People Think

But would Atlus opt for a Persona 6 blowout when Persona 4 Revival is just three months away from release? Admittedly, it does seem a bit counterintuitive from a marketing perspective — I've always been of a mind that the developer will kick the Persona 6 machine into gear once Revival is out.

Indeed, Persona Super Live 2027 takes place on 19th March, and to me, that felt like the ideal venue in terms of timing.

Having said that, it simply doesn't get bigger than The Game Awards — it's the most watched gaming event out there, and by a massive distance. All evidence points to Persona 6 launching at some point in 2027, and so Atlus won't be handed an opportunity like this again.

What do you think? Is Persona 6 a lock for The Game Awards, or will Atlus continue to hold fire — at least until Persona 4 Revival is out the door? Set unreal expectations in the comments section below.

#3996. The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

The Sims 4's Marketplace and user-created content have officially arrived on consoles, a little over a month after their debut on PC.

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

#3995. 'The Ultimate Gaming Machine' - Xbox Reveals Tons Of New Project Helix Information

Also clarifying that it's definitely a console and not a PC

As part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations today, we've been treated to a new digital version of a magazine that was given out at Seattle FanFest earlier this week, available to read in full over on the official Xbox Wire website.

The bit that's getting most attention concerns Xbox Project Helix - the new next-gen console that's currently in the works over at Xbox HQ. The brand's VP of Next Generation, Jason Ronald, shares tons of new information across four pages in the magazine, helping to give us a better idea of what to expect from the upcoming console.

There's one section in particular that's getting all the interest on social media right now, where he clarifies that Project Helix is definitely a console that can play PC games, and definitely not a PC that happens to play console games.

"We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Beyond this, Ronald talks in depth about loads of other aspects of what they're aiming for with Project Helix, and as mentioned, there's so much detail that it spreads across four pages of the magazine.

In the interest of highlighting as much as possible though, we thought we'd transcribe all of most notable quotes from the magazine down below, whereas you can read the added context inside of the magazine article itself.

Here are more of the key bits from the magazine article:

"When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine - one that removes all barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."

"We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics - it's really about gameplay innovation. It's about deeper immersion. It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering."

"When I think about what makes a console magical, it's that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don't have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings - things like that. The hardware and the experience is entirely designed around playing games."

"The very first next-generation conversations we had were with all of our first-party studios. That was absolutely foundational to the design of what we've done with Project Helix - talking about where they saw the future of game design going, where they saw the future of their franchises going, and what was constraining their creative ambition."

"With Xbox One, I think we got so focused on expanding our aperture that we lost sight of what truly is magical, which is players, developers, and the games that they love. We have to build the best platform for game developers to deliver their creative vision."

"The other thing, and I think this is something that is unique about Xbox, is we have to be connected to the community. A lot of the features that people have come to love and expect from Xbox have actually been driven directly by community feedback. I think that's really core to the soul of who Xbox is, because if you're in touch with your player base, you never go wrong if you focus on what their needs are."

"It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable."

"This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

"The ROG Xbox Ally was really an opportunity for us to learn alongside our player base with a lot of these concepts and the ideas that we had: being able to play libraries from across multiple different storefronts, understanding how PC games and console games can show up together in a unified library. The feedback that we've gotten from players has fundamentally informed and altered our plans of how it actually shows up in a future console. Players shared where we met the mark and areas we needed to improve or approach differently. So absolutely, we view the Ally as a precursor to what we're doing with Helix - but it's informed by a lot of the design concepts we have for Helix."

Sorry for the wall of quotes, but we thought you might find all of this pretty interesting! It's not even the full extent of what Ronald had to say, as he also touched on the importance of game preservation to the Xbox platform in general, as well as how Project Helix will seemingly have a bespoke UI, but one that still feels familiar to Xbox fans.

Of course, we're still waiting on concrete details about what Helix will look like, how much it'll cost, how significant the PC integration will be, and loads of other things that will give us a much better picture of how it'll shape up.

It seems like we won't be getting that this year though, and if rumours are to be believed, Xbox might even be releasing a first-party handheld in 2027 before the Project Helix console in 2028. Who knows... plans can always change.

For now, let us know what you think about this latest info on Xbox Project Helix down below, and we definitely recommend reading the full Xbox 25th anniversary magazine for yourself - we wish we could buy one to be honest!

Honestly, whilst any new information is welcome, there is not a lot to be learned here. I have 3 questions:

I'd like to know whether it has a disc-drive because I have an extensive Blu-ray film collection (2000+ films), and I currently use my Series X to play them. I'm not fussed about the capability to play physical games because I have been all digital since the beginning of the Xbox One era. If it does not come with a disc-drive, then one that can be added (much like with the PS5) would be good. It's not a deal breaker for me because I can always just buy a 4K Blu-ray player, but it would be better to have just Helix and a PS6 under my television, rather than a Blu-ray player as well.

I have a gaming PC that I do not use for gaming right now, so all I really want is for Helix to be a console that is more powerful than the Series X I already own. I want the simplicity of console gaming, not the complexity that PC gaming often brings.

Does it allow access to other storefronts?:

I have said so many times that I think Xbox allowing store fronts like Steam on Helix would be a massive mistake. Once people realise that even brand new games on Steam often cost £10 less upon release than they do on Xbox, and once they see how games are cut more deeply in sales on Steam than they are on consoles, they will soon begin to make Steam their dominant library, and that will cost Microsoft billions in lost revenue, and given how Xbox is doing right now, that could easily sound the death knell for Xbox. Xbox needs to be making more money, not losing more still by enabling consumers to buy their games on Steam etc..

The only other thing that I would like an answer to right now is when Helix will launch. Rumour has it that the PS6 will release next year, and if the other rumour doing the rounds about Helix releasing in 2028 is true, then Helix will sink without a trace unless it is massively more powerful than the PS6, and considerably cheaper than it too. Helix needs to release at the same time as the PS6, or preferably a year before it, for it to stand a chance of success, particularly if Helix is basically a console because then that does mean that both the PS6 and Helix could be more or less on par in terms of power. As a PC, then it was always expected that Helix would be considerably more powerful than the PS6, but if both are consoles, then they may be much closer to one another in terms of power, which will probably favour PlayStation given the current userbase imbalance. It's going to be a difficult balancing act for Xbox when it comes to power and capabilities versus pricing, and how that stacks up to the PS6, but whatever happens, I really do not think that Helix can allow the PS6 a years head start.

Those are the three biggest questions that I have for Helix. I'm not overly concerned about the price because I want Helix to be my primary gaming platform even though I will be buying a PS6 too. With any luck, we will hear a lot more details within the next 6 months (unless Helix is releasing in 2028, in which case it'll be more like 18 months)...

@Sol4ris Absolutely ! Xbox Helix will almost certainly be superior to the PS6. That's already pretty obvious in terms of power, the size of its game library, its services, the technologies it offers, and the level of freedom it provides, such as game modding.

At this point, the main advantage PlayStation may have left is price. We'll see whether the difference is significant or not, but considering Helix's advantages, if the price gap isn't huge, it will probably be well worth spending a bit more for a Helix.

There's also the battle over exclusive games. Xbox is expected to launch Helix with a strong lineup of exclusive titles, and the PS6 will likely do the same. But when you really think about it, even on that front PlayStation may already be at a disadvantage, since roughly 30-40% of the games available on Helix could be console exclusives to the platform, including not only Xbox first-party titles but also all the games that are released exclusively on PC, and there are a lot of those. Of course, that's talking about quantity and variety, which are already important advantages. The remaining question is game quality. And on that front, PlayStation needs to raise its game, because lately its first-party exclusives have not only been relatively few in number, but also haven't always lived up to expectations.

The next console war will also be decided by marketing and the public perception of the two brands. In that respect, PlayStation's reputation has taken quite a hit, while Xbox's image has become increasingly positive, particularly since Asha Sharma's arrival and the introduction of numerous player-friendly initiatives, such as Xbox Play Anywhere, lower Game Pass pricing, disc-to-digital support, a renewed focus on exclusive games, a stronger emphasis on consoles, the Rewards program, backward compatibility, and more.

These are all areas that distinguish Xbox from PlayStation, which, in comparison, doesn't seem to do much for its community other than ignore it.

#3994. "Essentially Worthless" - Disgruntled Fans Are Review Bombing Pikmin 4 On Switch 2

Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is out now, bringing 4K visuals to the 2023 title along with the new Dandori Academy mode and some neat little extras like voice commands.

We awarded it a score of 7/10 in our review. It's still good – hell, the main Pikmin 4 campaign is possibly the best of the bunch – yet we can't deny our disappointment at the lack of mouse controls and 60fps performance.

But if you take a look on Metacritic, you'd think Nintendo just put out its worst game in years. Although the metascore is sitting at a commendable 83, the game's user score is much, much lower at 2.3. This essentially means its average is 'Generally Unfavourable'. Yeesh.

Most folks just seem disgruntled at the notion that Nintendo is charging for what they perceive to be a very minor upgrade over the original. It's true that a lot of games over the years have received free updates for newer hardware, but Nintendo has opted to charge £7.99 / $9.99 / €9.99.

"This switch 2 edition is essentially worthless. At worst it's a spit in the face of series fans. $20 AUD for a bunch of recycled content and 4k visuals. They couldn't even be bothered to implement 60fps even though the system could definitely handle it. Such a lazy update, and yet they have the gall to charge $20 AUD."

Meanwhile, another user provided a slightly more measured assessment, stating:

"The Dandori Academy has reused content, half of the maps so far are taken directly from the base game and the other half share the same exact layout. Plus the new card on the title screen looks like an ad, ruins the nice scenery, fortunately it can be hidden.

"The main game has also suffered, now somehow having longer loading times than it did on the original Switch. All other Switch 2 editions have made them shorter, so this is really weird. It's not a small difference either, some have literally doubled."

The comment about the load times is particularly interesting.

This has been highlighted elsewhere, with YouTuber 'Press A!' posting an analysis titled 'Pikmin 4's DLC is a disaster...' (flexing that signature YouTube nuance right there) in which he compares the load times of the Switch 2 Edition with the original. When exiting out of a cave, the original would take around 6 seconds or so to load the main environment, however the same moment took over 30 seconds in the Switch 2 version.

A few people have mentioned the load times being quite long, so we tested it out ourselves. While loading into a cave takes about 6 seconds, loading out took around 14-15 seconds. Not the 30+ that others are citing, then, but probably long enough to raise an eyebrow or two.

Pikmin 4's user score on Switch 2 is a startling contrast to that of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Despite some concerns here and there regarding the game's overall difficulty and approachability compared to the original, Ocarina of Time commands the highest user score of all time at 9.6.

We'll be curious to see whether Nintendo takes any steps to improve the load times in Pikmin 4, but for what you actually get with the new content and visual enhancements on Switch 2, we'd say the upgrade price is probably appropriate. It'll tide us over until Pikmin 5, at least.

Review bombing as an act of protest is a valid act. As long as it stays within the boundaries of the piece of media that is being protested.

I think there’s an interesting distinction being overlooked here: the difference between the intensity of someone’s disappointment and the actual quality of what they’re reviewing.

Reviews don’t just exist to communicate with devs and publishers. They also help other consumers make informed decisions. When we start using scores primarily as a form of protest, we’re compromising that purpose.

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom charged $10 for its enhanced version, but at least the improvements felt very substantial. On the other hand, Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker received a free update that added features such as 4K resolution, HDR support, 60 FPS performance, and a co-op mode.

Super Mario Party Jamboree is probably the most disappointing example. The asking price felt difficult to justify given what was actually included, and the fact that Nintendo couldn't even deliver a 4K presentation makes the value proposition look even weaker. #3993. Palworld 1.1 and Palfarm updates are on hold because competing with GTA 6 is "not the best idea"

When half the waking world is playing something else, you have to take a hint

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The industry is on a go-slow this week, due to a certain new game from Rockstar's imminent arrival. As such, I wouldn't expect many updates from other popular releases, Palworld being among them, because it's just not a good time for headline space.

The main man for public relations on the Pokemon-inspired survival game states as much on Twitter. A fan chastised Pocketpair for not providing news on 1.1 and Palfarm, to whom the situation was plainly explained.

"Sharing news about Palworld 1.1 or Palfarm the week GTA 6 is about to drop is probably not the best idea," John 'Bucky' Buckley, head of communications and publishing at Pocketpair, says. "From a PR point of view!"

@RaiderNite Sharing news about Palworld 1.1 or Palfarm the week GTA6 is about to drop is probably not the best idea... :) From a PR point of view!November 17, 2026

The original tweeter agrees, but there's some division in the replies otherwise, because several people point out they're not Grand Theft Auto fans. Regardless, Buckley's statement is one of mere practicality.

The mainstream video games world is centered on the sixth mainline GTA right now. It's a release 13 years in the making, with an advertising budget to rival the GDP of a small country. Even the Weather Channel is doing sponsored posts.

This is not a good time to try and break ground on anything substantial for any other big games. Chances are high that some portion of your fanbase is distracted, and your coverage will be stifled because less resources are available for other projects and communities at the minute.

The GTA 6 storm will subside – it'll become background noise at some point. But release week? It's like putting another blockbuster film in cinemas around Avengers: Doomsday. You're just not going to get the same airplay. Palworld 1.1 and Palfarm updates will come, just not for the time-being.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Palworld devs get 5 days off to play GTA 6 – and after Pocketpair's CEO vanished to play Slay The Spire 2, I'd say that's probably wise.

#3992. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

#3991. Diablo 4's next season won't have any new mechanics or a new theme because all the focus is on Lord of Hatred

If you don't intend to buy the Lord of Hatred expansion, the next season in Diablo 4 won't be as exciting as you'd expect.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

#3990. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

#3987. "I Don't Feel This Is A Good Direction" - Chrono Trigger Composer Thinks It's Time To End Dragon Quest

"it’s no longer possible to create anything new"

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda has posted a blog in which he states it might be time for the Dragon Quest series to end.

As covered by our pals over at Time Extension, Mitsuda-san believes that without Akira Toriyama – who sadly passed away in 2024 – the Dragon Quest franchise cannot continue imitating the iconic artist's signature style.

The catalyst for this comment was the release of a new mobile game titled Dragon Quest RPG: The Cursed Tree And the Chosen Isle, which features artwork strikingly similar to Toriyama-san's work.

“Dragon Quest RPG‘s Toriyama-san-styled illustration has become a hot topic, but for the illustrator, for Akira Toriyama fans, and for the now-deceased Akira Toriyama himself, I don’t feel this is a good direction for everyone involved. In my personal opinion, since it’s no longer possible to create anything new no matter how hard one tries, it might be time to end the Dragon Quest series, and for Yuji Horii to create a new RPG. (There are a lot of remakes out there, after all).”

Online speculation, highlighted by Power Up Gaming, also points at the potential involvement of generative AI to create the in-game characters. However, despite enthusiasm around the technology from creator Yuji Horii, there's doesn't seem to be any legitimate evidence that this is the case.

Regardless, Mitsuda-san does have a point. Dragon Quest is synonymous with Toriyama-san's art style, and it might be tricky to maintain this without the man himself at the helm. Indeed, reaction to Dragon Quest XII: Beyond Dreams hasn't exactly been universally positive, with some online users criticising the design of the main protagonist.

We think it's unlikely that Dragon Quest will end anytime soon, however. The series is still incredibly popular to this day, and continues to sell ludicrous numbers in Japan especially. Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World is scheduled to release on Switch 1 and 2 on 3rd December 2026.

News "It's Truly Astonishing" - Dragon Quest Creator Yuji Horii Made An AI-Generated Game In 30 Minutes

What do you make of Mitsuda-san's comments here regarding Dragon Quest? Should the series end? Or do you think it just needs to adopt a different art style going forward? Let us know.

[source procyon-studio.com, via timeextension.com]

Nintendo Life’s resident horror fanatic, when he’s not knee-deep in Resident Evil and Silent Hill lore, Ollie likes to dive into a good horror book while nursing a lovely cup of tea. He also enjoys long walks and listens to everything from TOOL to Chuck Berry.

Miyamoto eats babies and Namco Bandai is secretly operated by Stephen King's pet dog. The absurd claims I just made are worth reporting on according to this article's journalistic standards.

Dragon Quest had always been the collaboration of Yuji Horii (scenario and program), Akira Toriyama (character and monster design), and Koichi Sugiyama. Sugiyama passed some time after Dragon Quest XI's 2017 release, and his musical contributions for that title were notably more limited as he was in his late 80s. Toriyama's sudden passing in 2024 at 68 was a shock, with his last anime production Dragon Ball Daima yet to finish its broadcast run at that time. Yuji Horii himself is now 72 years old.

As I understand it, Dragon Quest XII features contributions, compositions, and designs from the late Sugiyama and Toriyama respectively, as DQXII was initially announced in 2021. Whilst Dragon Quest is no stranger to spin-offs, this definitely feels like the final main series entry, and it won't be possible to continue these works without passing on the series to someone else.

Dragon Ball hasn't ended with Toriyama's passing, after all. Toyotarou is Toriyama's chosen successor, and he has continued the Dragon Ball manga series with the Moro arc (The Galactric Patrol), which is getting an anime adaption. There was a time where I couldn't imagine a Mario or Zelda game without the involvement of Shigeru Miyamoto. But look where we are now.

One thing Nintendo has done beautifully and you really do have to give them credit for, is that they transitioned their Developer talent beautifully to the next generation of their staff. There has never been a gap in their mainline series where say, a new Mario game feel inconsistent with everything that came before. If I play Super Mario Bros Wonder and then go back and play Super Mario World, the only thing that has really changed is the technology and the evolution of ideas.

Over the years, they've slowly integrated fresh, young talent and ingrained into them the essence of their games. What makes a Zelda game, a Zelda game? When is a central game mechanic strong enough to have a full game based around it? And what makes Mario games so timeless and fun? These are all questions that I'm very certain they've posed to their new staff as they gradually handed them the reigns and trusted them more and more with every subsequent release.

There is a reason why nobody complains that Miyamoto essentially just works on Nintendo movies these days and only acts as a consultant for modern Mario games.

A game is not just a work of one or two people, but an entire collective staff. #3986. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.
