#3985. Walton Goggins doesn’t know Fallout's future, but is confident season 3 remains true to the games

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

Bringing all the latest movie news, features, and reviews to your inbox

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

The Ghoul actor waxes lyrical about Fallout's attention to detail

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Walton Goggins has said Fallout season 3 once again does right by the games – and is holding out hope for a fourth season to continue that trend.

"It's very personal, you know. I mean, my son is a gamer. I see exactly how and why he plays games. I'm not a gamer at all, but the game of Fallout has been around for such a long time. It's been a shared experience between parents and their children and friends for such a long time, but it holds a very special place in their heart," Goggins said at an awards screening attended by GamesRadar+.

"I think what they have responded to, at least what I've been told out on the road, is the reverence in which all of us approach the sacred nature of this game, and while still keeping it an original story in the canon of Fallout."

To that end, Goggins – who plays the Ghoul in the Prime Video series – name-checked some of those responsible for maintaining Fallout's accuracy towards its video game counterpart.

"Everybody behind the scenes, including Howard Cummings, who's our production designer, and [showrunners Geneva Robertson-Dworet and Jonathan Nolan], who play the game, are constantly putting Easter eggs into the show and exploring and reminding people the roots of this story… protecting the tonality of the kind of subversive humor and the satirical kind of elements of this show," Goggins said.

Goggins added, "I feel confident that we've done that in season three, and if we get the opportunity to come back for season four, that would continue to honor how sacred this is to people. It's not something that we take lightly."

With Fallout season 3 heading to the Rockies for the first time in franchise history, it appears there's no shortage of ideas that the post-apocalyptic series can use to thrive. But Goggins's recent social media activity – a goodbye of sorts to the Ghoul – had fans worried for both the fate of his character and whether the show would continue past the third season.

While that information is properly locked in the deepest vault at Amazon, Goggins's co-star Kyle MacLachlan may have revealed that Fallout season 3 will air from May. If Goggins's words ring true, we can perhaps hope for something truly S.P.E.C.I.A.L.

For more, check out the Fallout timeline and our ranking of the best Fallout games.

#3984. Wolverine PS5 Slashes Its Price for the First Time in Black Friday Sales

Sony has reduced the price on its biggest first-party game of 2026, Marvel's Wolverine, as part of its Black Friday offerings.

The superhero action title typically retails for $69.99/£69.99 on PS Store, but the digital version of the game has had a decent percentage slashed away.

Until 30th November, you can grab it for $49.69/£52.49, a reduction of -29%/-25%. That's not bad for a major PS5 exclusive that only released a couple of months ago.

In the land of physical games, it's good news for Marvel's Wolverine too. In the UK, the game is discounted at all the main retailers you'd expect; the cheapest I've seen is Amazon, where you can grab it for £33.32.

Some deals are cropping up in the US as well. For example, Best Buy is offering the game for 20 bucks off at $49.99.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

Black Friday itself isn't until 27th November, so it's possible the game will be reduced at other places as the day draws closer.

Sony has announced its Black Friday activities, cutting prices on certain hardware and accessories, as well as games and more.

A big part of all that is the PS Store's massive Black Friday sale, which is running now through to the end of the month. We've compiled more than 80 offers we reckon are worth considering — many of the games are cheaper than ever.

#3983. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

#3982. Guide: GTA 6 Release Times: All The Key Details Xbox Players Need To Know

It's finally here! We've officially reached the launch week of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, PS5 and even the Xbox One (kind of), 13 long years since the most recent entry in the series back in 2013.

With that in mind, we thought we'd put up a quick release times guide so you know exactly when you can start playing the game, and we've also thrown in a few extra details about what we're expecting for Xbox One players at launch.

So, here are all the deets you need to know for Thursday!

On this page: GTA 6 Release Times: All The Key Details Xbox Players Need To Know

The official GTA 6 release date is Thursday, November 19th. You may still see people playing it on Wednesday though, as depending on where you live, certain players will be getting access to it earlier than others.

GTA 6 releases at midnight local time around the world. This means you'll be able to start playing it on Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S and PS5 as soon as November 18th turns into November 19th in your region.

The only exception to the rule may be in countries with multiple time zones. For example, Rockstar seems to be classing "midnight" based around the EST time zone in the US, which would mean PST gets it at 9pm on the 18th.

Technically, yes. Due to the staggered rollout, players in New Zealand will be getting first access to GTA 6 at midnight in their time zone, which equates to 11am on November 18th here in the UK, and even earlier in the United States.

We urge caution around this, as Xbox's terms of service specifically state that you shouldn't switch regions unless you're actually located in the country you're switching to, but we'll leave the decision up to you.

News Xbox Fans Urge Caution Over New Zealand Trick For GTA 6, While Others Say It's A Non-Issue

"They literally told me this in person in Seattle at Xbox FanFest last week"

You may have noticed that we didn't mention Xbox One in the release times section up above, and that's because we don't quite know what's happening with it. In a nutshell, Xbox One players will be forced to use Xbox Cloud Gaming in order to get access to GTA 6, which in theory should require buying the game before access is granted.

There are too many unknowns ahead of launch about how this works though. Will cloud access be made available immediately? Will you be able to use the free-with-ads version of the cloud to play GTA 6, or will it require paying for the service? Is it just Xbox One that you can play it on, or will mobile and PC devices be supported too?

That's where we stand ahead of launch, so while GTA 6 definitely will be playable through the cloud on Xbox One in some form, it's probably best to wait until it's been released before handing over any money as things stand.

News GTA 6 Will Be Playable On Xbox One Through Xbox Cloud Gaming

Rockstar also confirms GTA 6 will run at 30FPS

Of course, we've already talked about the preload for GTA 6 and how anyone can download the game right now on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, regardless of whether they've actually bought it or not.

All that's left is to wait a few more days until the new Grand Theft Auto finally becomes available, and we can't wait to see whether it'll live up to the hype and become a Game of the Year contender when it arrives this Thursday.

News How To Preload GTA 6 In Full On Xbox Series X|S (Even If You Haven't Bought It)

All 200GB+ goes live in just a few hours' time

Yeah sure. I will use UK and NZ times for demonstrative purposes.

Let's say it's 11 am GMT. You can boot up your UK version via a change to the NZ timezone, as the unlock time will now be linked to the NZ store. (which will be 12 AM NZ) 13 hours early.

When you finish your play session - for example, at 8 pm GMT- you then need to change your time zone back from NZ to GMT on your Xbox. You then need to wait 13 hours and 1 minute before you can play and make another save. The system will think there is only 1 minute between save files rather than the 13 hours and 1 min that have passed. This prevents you from overwriting a save from what the system sees as the future.

#3981. Review: TANUKI: Pon's Summer (Switch 2) - Cosy Postie Delivers Sick BMX Tricks & Minigames

The gaming calendar is busier than it’s been in recent memory. We’re wedged between the Ocarina of Time remake and GTA 6, having only just recovered from the onslaught of games that launched in September. The prospect of picking up another right now might not be an inviting one, but if any game could do it, it’s Tanuki: Pon’s Summer.

This quiet, cosy, understated gem has really launched at the perfect time. Playing as the titular Tanuki, you’re tasked with getting a shrine ready for a big festival towards the end of the summer. You have to raise funds for repair work, and find folks in town who can actually carry it out. To do so, you pick up a delivery job, get to know all of your eccentric neighbours, and pull off some sick BMX tricks along the way.

That sounds simple, but this is just the ramp used to propel you into the ridiculous amount of tasks you can get up to in Tanuki: Pon’s Summer. While primarily all about riding a BMX and delivering parcels, you quickly realise that this is a simulation game with a vibrant, animated world that invites exploration.

A quirk of the delivery outfit you work for is that you don’t just deliver the mail. No, you are the backbone of society. The job isn’t over until the customer has a smile on their face. So, if your round takes you to a local fisherman, and he’s feeling down about how he isn’t getting enough business, it’s your job to cheer him up and try out some fishing yourself. If you’re dropping a parcel off at a bar, and the place is packed, you better get ready to pull pints. If a photographer is lacking inspiration, then you have to pick up a camera and help her find it.

You get the point; Tanuki: Pon’s Summer manages to pull off so many wildly different minigames with ease, and (mostly) without losing its identity. When you park up the BMX to play some baseball, it feels like you’re diving further into this gorgeous world, rather than stepping into a different game entirely.

It feels like the idea behind these minigames is that they’re not supposed to overstay their welcome, but I found myself sorely wishing I could return to a few of them. The golf minigame towards the end in particular is one of the best golf sims going. The same goes for bar work; trying to replicate the drinks being ordered was satisfying and moreish, but gone too soon and never playable again. If anything, developer Denkiworks misses a trick in not giving you some kind of game mode that lets you play through these on a loop - I would have happily dived back in for that.

This is not to say that every minigame is pulled off with ease. There are some that just don’t work, and were more of a frustrating slog than anything else. The good thing is that this is a cosy game with low stakes, so if you’re struggling with one of them, there’s almost always a way to make things more generous, or skip over it if you fail enough times. But at times, this can feel like a cop out; the few frustrating minigames could have been improved rather than skipped over.

Unfortunately, the worst game of the bunch doesn’t even let you skip it, at least in my playthrough. This involves you transporting boulders in a cave, rolling them through an obstacle course.

To understand the issue with this, you have to understand that Tanuki: Pon's Summer doesn’t do precise controls. The opening makes this clear when you’re taught how to use the BMX - everything is simplified, and you’re not expected to do anything too intricate. Pon moves around too sluggishly and ragdoll-y for that to work. And for the most part, the game is built around this.

The cave minigame forgets this entirely. Pon has to pilot the boulders through tight walkways, often fighting against the game’s physics to avoid falling off the ledge. If you do fall, you go right back to the beginning, losing all progress. I got through it, but I worried for the state of my Joy-Con afterwards, with how much stress they were put through.

Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is at its best when it’s as difficult as you want it to be. You can try and pull off some tricks in golf to beat your opponent, or play it safe and have her win. You can make a lousy bartender and call it a day, or you can throw your all into it. You can rack up as many points on the BMX as you like, or ride slow and steady. But when a minigame just can’t find its footing, like riding the boulders in the cave, the game loses track of what makes it work.

At times, it can also feel that the game spreads itself a little too thin. I felt this most in the basic base building. You can unlock a whole lot of items to revamp the Tanuki shrine, but you can’t do too much with them. There’s just not enough freedom, so the plots of land became more of a dumping ground for my trophies.

Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is a cosy game that understands what it means to be a cosy game: create a gorgeous world you want to get lost in, with satisfying but lower-stakes gameplay. By the time I had rebuilt the Tanuki shrine and completed Pon’s summer job, I wanted to dive back in and see more of the townsfolk I’d met along the way. I wanted to keep delivering their mail and nosing my way into their business.

But there were a few sequences in the game I was happy to see the back of, either because they were on the duller side, or just didn’t work with the exaggerated, slapstick control scheme. Equally, I wish Pon’s Summer spent longer on what it does right, letting us go on an infinite number of deliveries around the island, or play as much golf as we please.

#3980. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#3979. Grammy Awards Reveal This Year's Nominees for Best Video Game Soundtrack

The nominees for the 2027 Grammy Awards were recently announced, and of particular interest to gamers will be the shortlist for Best Score Soundtrack For Video Games and Other Interactive Media.

Five games, released between 31 August, 2025 and 28th August, 2026, are in contention, and two of them come from Sony's first-party efforts.

This could be a second Grammy for Gordy Haab, who jointly won for his work on Star Wars Jedi: Survivor in the 2024 awards.

PS Studios almost always has very strong music, so it's no surprise to see some representation here. Personally I can't speak to Marvel's Wolverine, but the score for Ghost of Yotei is great.

As for 007 First Light, to be honest I struggle to recall any of the music aside from the Bond theme and Lana Del Ray's title track.

It's an interesting group, anyway — I'm not sure I could really call it.

This will be only the fifth time the category has appeared at the Grammy Awards. Here are the previous winners if you're interested:

#3978. Nintendo's 'Switch 2 Holiday Experience' Might Be Coming To A City Near You Next Month (US)

Nintendo's making sure that everyone has a Switch 2 on their wishlist this Christmas, as it has today announced the 'Nintendo Switch 2 Holiday Experience', which will be coming to select cities in the US over the next month.

Running from 25th November to 23rd December, the pop-up will feature playable demos for a bunch of Switch 2's finest (Pokopia, Mario Kart World, Ocarina of Time, Splatoon Raiders, and more), and give you a chance to see them all in both handheld and docked mode.

The event will also feature a Nintendo Holiday Gift Guide — because you know kids will leave this one wanting a console of their own — and all attendees can 'check in' at the My Nintendo station to redeem a gift tag set and 100 Platinum Points.

Here's where you'll find the 'Holiday Experience' between 25th Nov and 23rd Dec:

Is it all yet another excuse for kids to annoy their parents about how much they "need" a Switch 2 on the run-up to Christmas? Probably. But hey, the more people that get a chance to play Ocarina of Time, the better.

#3977. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 will take us deeper into the World in Canvas and make Mortenax Blade playable

Honkai: Star Rail's next big outing will see the continuation of the Planarcadia story, and it's going to be with us soon.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

#3976. DOOM: The Dark Ages Revelations Gets A Major Free 'Slaughter Mode' Update Today

The release of DOOM: The Dark Ages Revelations saw critics heaping praise on the expansion earlier in 2026, to the point where it's actually even in the Game of the Year (or at least Expansion of the Year) conversation as things stand.

News Xbox Has Another Potential GOTY Candidate On Its Hands, Even Though It's Just DLC

The reviews for Revelations have been absurdly good

The DLC is getting even better today as well, as a new November 16th updating is introducing "Slaughter Mode - an endless combat challenge in which you need to tear through waves of hordes and unlock rewards along the way.

DOOM developer id Software says no two runs in Slaughter Mode are identical due to the random encounters it throws at you, and there will also be special unlockable skins and weekly challenges thrown into the mix.

"Complete rounds to earn Skulls, which unlock rewards such as Slaughter Mode-only Slayer skins, weapon skins for all modes and profile icons. You can also unlock tracks from Andrew Hulshult’s IDKFA soundtrack to play in both Slaughter Mode and the Ripatorium! Take on weekly challenges for more opportunities to earn rewards and show off your slaying prowess."

All of this is available to you if you own the Revelations DLC for DOOM: The Dark Ages already, or if you have the Premium / Premium Upgrade versions of DOOM: The Dark Ages.

Don't forget that the base game is currently included with Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, Premium and PC Game Pass as well, so if you just want the DLC to play on Game Pass, you're looking at paying £17.99 / $19.99 for it.

We'll leave you with more details about the new Slaughter Mode for DOOM The Dark Ages: Revelations below.

Tear through relentless, escalating and unpredictable waves of demonic hordes, carving out your personal best scores and unlocking rewards using the Skulls collected from the carnage. With each checkpoint reached, players must ask themselves if they want to cash in their run or risk it all for more slaughter. No two runs through Slaughter Mode are identical as you fight escalating rounds of random encounters, bosses and arenas, turning up the heat as you proceed further into your run.

#3974. Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

After a long wait and exhaustive leaks, the highly-anticipated Simpsons event will finally arrive in Monopoly Go very soon, alongside new content.

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

#3973. Mini Review: Tanuki: Pon's Summer (PS5) - Easily One of 2026's Most Charming Adventures

Tanuki: Pon's Summer is a delight — and a finely crafted delight at that.

This is one of the most downright lovable indies I've played in a long time; it's a consistently charming concoction of semi-open world exploration, character stories, and minigames.

You play as the titular Pon, a lazy little tanuki who's tasked with repairing his god's shrine for the upcoming festival. But this is the kind of work that requires cash, and so our unlikely protagonist somehow snags a job at the local post office.

What follows is a day-to-day adventure across a rural Japanese island, where Pon must deliver packages to its inhabitants, and often lend a paw to their predicaments.

Oh, and Pon's also a BMX enthusiast, which means that he can take advantage of the landscape's many bike ramps and grinding rails to get around more (or less) efficiently.

There's a whole trick system that you can master, and while far from mandatory, pulling off sick moves as you go about your business nets you extra money at the end of your shift. Additional moolah lets you purchase more decorations for your shrine — which you're free to customise when you're not at work.

The relaxed process of cycling around the island, meeting quirky new characters, and taking part in an impressive variety of minigames — like fishing, bug catching, pint pouring, sushi stacking, and many others — is surprisingly moreish.

Indeed, developer Denkiworks has created something quite special in terms of structure. It feels like the game's always coming up with clever new ways to keep you entertained, which makes for a very nicely paced package.

That said, a few of the minigames can come across as slightly tedious. Picking up trash or sanding the bark off logs, for example, can't compare with landing a big fish, or partaking in a spot of sumo. Still, as alluded, it's hard to fault the variety that's on offer.

Lovingly put together and full of heart, Tanuki: Pon's Summer is a fantastic little slice of relaxation.

#3972. GDC Survey Suggests Devs Want To Make Games For Switch 2 More Than PS5 Or Xbox

The GDC Festival of Gaming has published its latest 'State of the Game Industry' report, which is based on a survey of over 2,600 game industry professionals on topics such as AI, layoffs, labour, and more.

One particular result caught our eye, and it's regarding which platforms developers are currently interested in developing for in the future. As expected, PC was comfortably the winner at 81%, likely down to its versatility, ease-of-use, and broad visibility of storefronts like Steam and Epic Games Store.

However, it's the Switch 2 that bagged the silver medal at 46%, putting it ahead of the PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Steam Deck, Steam Machine, and even upcoming consoles like the PS6 and Project Helix.

Since its release in June 2025, the Switch 2 has seen a staggering number of releases, from high-profile 'AAA' titles to smaller indie games, and it seems this is only set to continue or perhaps even accelerate in the future.

In a similar chart looking at which platform(s) developers' upcoming game or project will ship on next, the Switch 2 ranks lower than PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Steam Deck, pulling in 29% of the vote. With this one, however, it's worth considering external factors that might be at play.

For example, it's easy to say that you want to develop for the Switch 2, but whether you have the budget and dev kits to actually do so is another question. Just something to consider when looking at these results.

#3971. Something Weird Is Going On With GoldenEye 007 And Xbox Game Pass

Earlier this month, you may recall that Xbox announced 14 games that would be leaving Game Pass in early November, with arguably the highlight of the bunch being the classic Rare FPS, GoldenEye 007.

We initially thought this might have been a mistake, but then Xbox doubled-down by announcing the game's departure in an official Xbox Wire roundup, confirming that it would definitely be leaving console and cloud on November 15th.

We're now on November 16th, and GoldenEye 007 remains included with Game Pass. Every other title from the list has been removed from the service, but Bond has defied the odds once again to remain part of the subscription!

So, what's going on here? It might take a while until we find out for sure, but we're going to guess that Xbox has either managed to arrange a deal to keep GoldenEye 007 on Game Pass, or they've just pushed back the removal date.

In any case, it's weird that nobody's said anything about this yet, and we're hoping we'll get clarification in the near future. GoldenEye has always been a game that's been tied up in licensing issues (hence why we never got the cancelled Xbox 360 version of it), but perhaps they've managed to figure out a long-term solution.

Anyway, we'll keep an eye on it, and this article will be updated with any important information that's revealed over the next few days. For now though, feel free to keep enjoying GoldenEye 007 on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and Premium!

#3970. The Great Star Wars: Galactic Racer Will Soon Be Even Better, Major New Features Announced

While Star Wars: Galactic Racer is an excellent arcade racing game in many respects, it did launch with a few missing features that left some speed freaks a little disappointed.

However, it seems developer Fuse Games is keen to address those concerns, as it's just announced a couple of much-requested modes are officially in the works.

Announced via social posts, Galactic Racer is getting local split-screen multiplayer as well as Free Play mode:

Fuse Games says these new features are planned to arrive in "early 2027" and are currently being worked on within a "dedicated team."

As the work-in-progress screenshot shows, Galactic Racer will support four-player local multiplayer; there's no footage yet, so it's unknown how that's going to perform, but hopefully it can uphold the game's silky smooth frame rate.

Free Play, meanwhile, will be the home for split-screen, as well as other race types. "This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action," the post reads.

I'm really glad the studio is implementing these features in the new year. While Galactic Racer has plenty to enjoy already, I think the ability to make your own custom races is a logical next step.

To be honest, I wasn't expecting any split-screen support at all, but I'm pleased to be proven wrong there.

#3969. "Pressure To Go For The Cheaper Option Grows" - XSEED Reckons Game-Key Cards Are Here To Stay

"The end of physical media was declared many years ago"

Amongst the Switch 2's many Game-Key Card physical releases in its first year, Marvelous USA/XSEED has stood firm as one of the few third-party publishers consistently offering complete-on-card releases. Nintendo's new smaller cart option may entice more studios to follow suit, but XSEED CEO Ken Berry can't see the format going away any time soon.

In a new RPG Site interview all about the state of physical media in 2026, Berry admitted that it's actually "getting harder" for publishers to bring 'proper' physical releases to Switch 2, as GKCs are "getting more and more accepted," leading to a growing "pressure to go for the cheaper option".

He continues that despite smaller cart options coming into play, there's still a hefty amount of uncertainty when it comes to component pricing:

Future uncertainty on pricing on anything that contains computer chips due to what’s affectionately called the ongoing RAMpocalypse would point to disc-based or Game-Key Card releases as maybe having even a greater cost advantage in the future.

It's not something that Marvelous/XSEED is using itself, mind you. The publisher released proper physical editions for Rune Factory: Guardians of Azuma, Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar and Daemon x Machina: Titanic Scion in North America last year, and is continuing that with Muramasa: Revenant Blades, Fate/Extra Record and Eternal Anima in 2027 (some of which will receive a GKC release in other regions).

"The end of physical media was declared many years ago, but we continued to see strong demand for them, especially the premium SKUs such as limited editions," Barry says. "But I would say in the past year or two it has really shifted where, after the initial shipment of units goes out at launch, even if it sells through to the end consumers really well, we don’t get the kind of reorders from retailers to restock their inventory the way we used to."

By the sound of things, Barry seems convinced to keep the physical releases going for as long as possible in North America — he notes that things can be more "challenging" in the EU thanks to "All the different countries and languages they have to accommodate". And long may it continue!

While Nintendo apparently has its smaller 32GB cards now available, it'll take continued appetite for full on-cart releases to convince publishers that they are worthwhile.

#3968. Xbox Creates New Website That Generates You A Doctor's Note For GTA 6

And teams up with DJ Khaled in the process

Xbox is having a bit of fun with the GTA 6 launch this week, even if they're not allowed to officially market it in some situations (due to an apparent deal struck between Take-Two and PlayStation). For example, they've just created a doctor's note website for the game, but it's not spelt out that it's for GTA 6.

It obviously is for the new Grand Theft Auto though, and they've even teamed up with music star DJ Khaled to help promote this random new website. In a nutshell, if you head over to DrXbox.com, you can enter your name and get a generated doctor's note that says you're suffering from "Vitamin G deficiency".

Here's a closer look (via Tom Warren on social media):

It's obviously just a bit of fun that won't hold up in any self-respecting business, but you could at least give it a try if they have a sense of humour! Probably best to just book the day off though - it's the kind of game that deserves it.

Anyway, go and have a play with this website if you want to. We find it a little bit weird and random to have partnered with DJ Khaled for something like this, but it gave us a chuckle at least.

Everything including 'creating and deleting single-player characters' can be done without touching the web.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

At long last, the transfer of power is complete. Dune: Awakening, Funcom's ambitious survival MMO based on the classic sci-fi novel, has completed is pivot away from massive multiplayer, and can now be played fully offline.

The offline function arrived in an otherwise unremarkable patch that mainly fixes specific bugs and technical issues. "It's now possible to play the game in single-player mode without requiring an internet connection at any point, including creating and deleting single-player characters.," Funcom revealed in a Steam post.

Dune: Awakening has been gradually drifting away from being a purely multiplayer experience for some time. In April, Funcom made its PvP element, like the Deep Desert and shipwreck exploration, fully optional. A fully fledged single-player mode arrived in September, including a dramatic rework of several major endgame systems—like its dynamic political "Landsraad" system' to make them work in solo play. At that point, single-player still required an Internet connection. Now though, that's no longer the case.

To be clear, Dune: Awakening can still be played with all its multiplayer and PvP trappings, now including a "Go Online" button for exactly that purpose. Nonetheless, it's been a fascinating shift in direction, one that, alongside games like Marathon, embodies a broader apparent trend away from large-scale. competitive multiplayer experiences toward smaller, cooperative communities. Whether with friends or alone, players increasingly want to be able to live in their own worlds, unbothered by the wider, more tumultuous encounters of the open Internet.

Whether this is a positive shift is up for debate—encounters with strangers on the Internet can provide highs as well as lows—but it's certainly an interesting one. Either way, offline mode isn't the end of Dune: Awakening's journey. A new expansion is coming in December, one that lets players explore Arrakis' frozen poles in a radically different scenario from the base game. Funcom appears to be in it for the long term with Awakening too, having recently pivoted to focusing purely on support for it and its other multiplayer survival game Conan: Exiles.

#3965. Xbox CEO Pens New Message, Urges Platform Not To Get 'Trapped' By Its Proud History

Yesterday, we talked about the Project Helix part of the Xbox 25th anniversary magazine that's been made available to read in full on the official Xbox Wire website, and there's plenty more interesting stuff where that came from!

For example, the magazine kicks off with a statement from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who discusses the past 25 years of the brand and where it's going in the future - similar to a statement she shared on social media recently.

This time though, she talks less about how games will be made, and more about the fact that she wants to take "creative risks" while also acknowledging that her team won't "get every decision right" along the way.

"There are plenty of milestones from the past 25 years, and you'll find many of them in these pages. But I don't think the story of Xbox is really a story about any given hardware, launch or number. It is a story about people. Players turned games into friendships, rivalries and family traditions. They played with roommates who became lifelong friends, with brothers and sisters who moved across the country, with parents who got older and kids who eventually picked up the controller themselves. Some of the people we played with 25 years ago are no longer here. Some are sitting next to us, now playing with a new generation."

"We should be proud of that history. But we shouldn't be trapped by it."

"Games are alive. The best ones find new players and new creators. They move between generations. They get changed, remade and occasionally broken apart and rebuilt into something nobody expected. Twenty-five years in, Xbox should have that same restlessness."

"We have been given the chance to care for some of the most loved games and characters in the world. Our job is to protect what makes them special without protecting them from change. To keep making new things. To take creative risks. To meet players wherever they choose to play. And to make sure someone discovering Xbox for the first time today can feel the same possibility that someone felt turning on that first console in 2001."

"We don't get every decision right. No company that is still making things does. But we can keep listening, learning and building. Twenty-five years ago, a relatively small group of people imagined that Microsoft could make a game console. It was an improbable idea. They made it real. I like that as our inheritance."

There's definitely some interesting stuff in here, including Sharma's insistence that Xbox shouldn't be "trapped" by its past, that her team should be willing to experiment and take risks in the future, and an admission that not every decision will work out for the best. That's pretty refreshing to hear, and it certainly reads well on paper at least.

Let's see what happens, eh? Xbox's 25th anniversary has been a weird year, full of ups and downs, but it seems like there's a cautious optimism circulating around the fanbase regarding things like console updates, exclusives and various other initiatives that have been introduced since the Xbox CEO took the helm at the start of the year.

These next 25 years are going to be fascinating to say the least!

#3964. Civilization Developer Firaxis Games Cuts A Third Of Its Staff, Studio Head Departs

A new report from Bloomberg reveals that Firaxis Games, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, has cut around one third of its staff. Meanwhile, its studio head Heather Hazen will also depart.

Approximately 60 people have been laid off as work on a new XCOM stalled over the Summer, with the game reportedly missing a huge milestone. Development will continue, but it will likely be met with a pretty drastic shake-up.

A spokesperson for 2K, a subsidiary of Take-Two, shared the following statement:

“Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength — designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis.

"These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

Funny how they try to spin these statements to make it sound almost positive, eh?

Firaxis most recently released Civilization VII for the Switch and Switch 2, amongst other major platforms. Reception was fairly mixed, but it received a solid 8/10 from us upon its release on the Switch 1. Since then, it's received numerous updates, but it's arguably failed to achieve the same success as earlier entries.

It's particularly egregious that this should come just a couple of days before the release of GTA 6, another Take-Two title developed by Rockstar Games. It's set to be one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time, but it seems Take-Two felt the need to save even more money elsewhere.

I could claim that I love real-time strategy games for their fast-paced decision-making. But what I truly love is building massive armies and wreaking havoc on an apocalyptic scale. So when I saw the trailer for Horu (via RPS), an in-development RTS that promises "hundreds of thousands of units" on screen, it went on the wishlist faster than you can say 'Zerg Rush'.

Horu is an upcoming strategy game inspired by Total War and Star Wars: Empire at War, aiming to blend the colossal battles of the former with the galaxy-scale strategy of the latter. It challenges players to establish their own interstellar empire, building vast space fleets and huge land armies to assume ultimate dominion of the cosmos.

While it's the spectacle of Horu that caught my attention, with clouds of spaceships trading laser fire and oceans of little men getting obliterated by artillery, there are a couple of more specific ideas and mechanics that also sound deeply exciting. Unlike the games that inspired it, Horu aspires to be fully real-time, with battles playing out simultaneously across the solar system. This includes both land and space battles, letting you do things like punch your dropships through an enemy's orbital fleet to land an army on the surface while the battle in space rages on.

This sounds rad, but also like it might be challenging to keep track of. Thankfully, Horu promises a few mechanics to keep the scale manageable. This includes a "drop zone system" that lets you assign a drop zone on a planet and queue up a set of orders, which the assigned army will then carry out automatically.

Other planned features include world colonisation and development, the ability to build spy networks and conduct espionage missions, space magic that'll let you cast devastating spells on the battlefield, and a fully simulated economy and research tree. There's even a system that lets you create boarding parties to take control of enemy ships and add them to your fleet.

All of this built by a solo dev who goes by GlassBeaver, who built his own custom engine to develop the game. Development has been underway for several years, but GlassBeaver has now taken the game to Kickstarter "to help fun the remaining assets, sound and music". The campaign is already halfway to reaching its goal of £16,685, so it looks likely to get over the finish line.

There's no specific release date for Horu yet, but GlassBeaver plans for the game to launch at the end of 2027. The next 12 months are shaping up to be big for space strategy more broadly, with Dawn of War 4 due to launch in December, and Total War: Warhammer 40,000 expected sometime next year.

#3962. 'We've Heard You!' - Star Wars Galactic Racer Is Officially Adding Split-Screen Multiplayer

An incredible addition to an incredible game

Star Wars Galactic Racer is my favourite game of the year so far. It's an incredible racing title that even surpasses the original Star Wars Episode 1 Racer in my view, and I've had so much fun with the campaign and online multiplayer.

There's just one downside that everyone's been pointing out since it was revealed, and that's the absence of local split-screen multiplayer. With that in mind, the development team have found a way to implement it in a new update.

The update isn't available yet, but will be coming to the game in early 2027. Alongside it will be a new mode called Free Play, which is where you'll be able to freely choose your vehicle, character, planet and race track.

"We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action."

It seems Free Play is the only place where you'll be able to access local split-screen multiplayer in Star Wars Galactic Racer, but that's no surprise considering how solo-focused the main campaign is. They'd literally have to rewrite massive portions of the campaign if they were going to implement split-screen into it.

Anyway, this is just an amazing bonus on top of an already amazing game, and I encourage you to check it out if you enjoy a title like Burnout 3: Takedown - it's fast-paced and frantic, has the same kind of takedown system that you'll remember from that game, and the roguelite campaign is really well designed (online is great fun as well).

If you've played it, let us know what you think of the game in the poll down below!

You are at, I don't know, some sort of family dining experience. There is a stage. On the stage, there is a magician. You are called up, and made to select a card from a deck of 52. "Don't show me, don't show me", exclaims the sorcerer. There is a dramatic pause, and then he reveals—from his own pocket—your card. Polite applause.

He keeps going: from his other pocket, your wallet. From his shirt, your wedding ring. Under his hat, your pet hamster, clutching in its teeth a love letter you wrote to your wife when you were first dating. The magician removes his mask—he is you, and you are your wife. Also, throughout this process, someone has given you a backpack and keeps adding exotic hammers to it.

This is what playing Queen's Domain feels like.

Developed, somehow, by a team of two developers, Queen's Domain is a game of constant discoveries. From the moment you wash ashore on the Isle of Neasied, the game just keeps unfurling. It is like some monstrous origami—you unfold one part only to find within it 10 more seemingly impossible sub-folds. Within those? You know it, baby: sub-sub-folds. We are through the looking glass here.

All of Queen's Domain's levels are riddled with crevices, crannies, nooks, and hideaways. Going through them is an experience in seeing some distant ledge, suspiciously flat bit of wall, or oddly aligned geometry and asking yourself "Could I…?" You can. You almost always can, and the game's levels reward your ingenuity and curiosity with new weapons, stat buffs, and strange encounters with stranger NPCs.

Sometimes you unlock whole new regions. Sometimes this is not good. Requiescat in pace to all those who fell down a well and found themselves stranded forever in a beautiful but deadly zone they were approximately 40 levels too underpowered for.

It is the best Dark Souls 1 since Dark Souls 1: unforgiving but almost never unfair, except when being unfair would be funny, and forever dazzling you with masterstrokes of interwoven level design. 16 hours in and hacking my way through a major dungeon, I pulled a lever only to open a door that spat me out right at the game's starting area. I suspect a cross-section of this game's goliath, entwined map would make for a killer bit of wall art.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Also, you kill like a billion things. Neasied and its sub-environs are filled with freaky creatures—including a fun screeching loot goblin—and it's up to you to put an end to them, which you do via the mechanism of your heaving sack of wunderwaffen. Here is where I warn you, reader: you might be a bit put off by the way Queen's Domain's combat functions at first.

It starts out stiff, stubborn, and idiosyncratic. Even basic enemies take a while to kill and you don't yet have all the tools to deal with them, mobility included. Meanwhile, mechanics like damage being commensurate with your stamina and every single enemy having a rock-paper-scissors-esque relationship to the game's damage types (they're weak to one, neutral to another, and resistant to a third) gives you a whole lot to think about as you try to figure out how to position yourself and swap between weapons without getting murdered.

Stick with it. It's the Morrowind thing: you need that first half hour (and it really is barely more than that) of struggle to appreciate the way your power scales as you unlock new weapons, acquire more abilities, and—most important—your understanding of the game deepens.

And if that doesn't tempt you, how about this: you like Pokémon? Because it's Pokémon, except your Pokémon are spears and clubs and mauls. You level every weapon independently from your own character level, and when they get high enough, a lot of them literally evolve, like Squirtle, into something new and weird.

At one point in my playthrough, I got stuck in an area for like three hours (I missed something obvious), and didn't even mind; it gave me time to level all three of the game's starting weapons into their bizarre, magical final forms.

I tell you, nothing has smitten me in 2026 like this. It is undoubtedly my personal game of the year, and it might be the first time I've felt that magic I first felt 13 years ago, ensconced in a first-year university flat, playing Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition on my PC for the first time.

#3960. Ocarina Of Time, Pokopia, Fire Emblem & More Pick Up The Game Awards 2026 Nominations

We are rapidly approaching the arrival of The Game Awards on 10th December, and today, Geoff Keighley has announced all of the nominees for this year's show.

While the weight of GTA 6 cast its shadow over most categories (come on, it's not even out yet!), Nintendo picked up a good number of nominations itself, including a spot in the all-important GOTY top six for Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Heck, it's the most-nominated publisher this year with 12 nods all to itself — overtaking the likes of Capcom (11), Annapurna Interactive (9) and PlayStation (9)

Link's latest is joined by 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Grand Theft Auto 6, Phantom Blade 0 and Resident Evil Requiem in the running for this year's top prize.

Here are all of the Nintendo games that have been nominated for the 2026 show, accompanied by the categories in which they'll appear:

On the Nintendo-related side of things, Switch 2 exclusive Orbitals picked up nominations in the Best Multiplayer Game and Best Debut Game categories, and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie is nominated for the Best Adaptation Award.

You'll find the full list of this year's nominees on The Game Awards' website. The full awards show will be livestreamed on YouTube on 10th December.

Do you reckon Nintendo will take home any of the above awards? Who will win GOTY? Let us know in the comments.

#3959. GTA 6's 'Unpredictable' Microclimate Revealed by The Weather Channel, with New PS5 Screenshots

GTA 6’s marketing has kicked into overdrive days ahead of its PS5 release, with even The Weather Channel offering an exclusive look into Leonida’s microclimate.

In a viral social media post, the US TV network said “nobody knows weather like we do [so] that’s why Rockstar gave us an exclusive look at the forecast for Leonida”.

Owen Shepherd, who worked on lighting and rendering in the game, explained that Florida – the state the game is based on – has one of the most “unpredictable weather systems in the US”.

“To match the fidelity of all aspects of what is the deepest, most immersive take on the Grand Theft Auto series yet, we had to completely reimagine our in-game weather systems to feel more localised, persistent, and above all dynamic. Weather can range with everything from clear blue skies to towering vertiginous cumulonimbus clouds, grounding players in a world through weather we hope Florida locals – and new visitors to Leonida – can appreciate.”

New PS5 screenshots show off the range of weather scenarios that can occur, including driving rain, dense sea fog, dramatic thunder storms, and ethereal mist.

It all looks remarkably impressive, doesn’t it? Just a few more days, folks.

#3958. Andy Serkis once had a "falling out" with Elijah Wood because he treated his Lord of the Rings scenes like a "rehearsal"

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

Lord of the Rings stars Andy Serkis and Elijah Wood didn't start off on the best terms, but the Gollum star says he's "like family" now

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In just over one year, we will see original Lord of the Rings stars Andy Serkis, Elijah Wood, and Ian McKellen reunite in The Hunt for Gollum. However, despite now thinking of the original cast as family, Serkis didn't always feel at home in Middle-earth.

In an interview with Radio Times, Serkis revealed that at the beginning of filming Peter Jackson's trilogy, he often felt "lonely" and like "an outsider” on set. "Everyone else had already been out in New Zealand for months before I arrived. They’d already bonded. So there was a sense of separation between them and me," said Serkis.

The Smeagol star said he and hobbit actors Elijah Wood and Sean Astin had a bit of a tiff at one point. "It wasn’t really a falling-out," said Serkis, "Well, it was a falling-out. Because of the new way we were using motion capture to film Gollum, when we were shooting scenes together, they were treating them almost like a rehearsal. So there were harsh words. But once we understood each other, we were golden."

Serkis was introduced as the cave dweller in 2001's The Fellowship of the Ring, before returning to the character in The Two Towers, The Return of the King, and in The Hobbit prequels. However, due to Serkis playing a goblin of sorts, Gollum was created via motion capture, meaning Serkis was on set wearing an optical suit. This kind of technology was pretty new at the time, which explains Wood and Astin reaction.

That is all water under the bridge now, as Serkis, Wood, and Gandalf star McKellan are back together to make The Hunt for Gollum. "It’s like family," said Serkis. Wood shares the feeling, as earlier this year he told GamesRadar+, "It's sort of like getting the band back together… It feels like a family reunion. My part to play is relatively small, but I'm just excited to go back and spend some time in New Zealand and see old friends."

The Hunt for Gollum takes place between The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings trilogies, before Frodo and the Fellowship start their quest to destroy the One Ring. Serkis confirmed that the movie is "over a week away from starting principal photography," adding that Aragorn actor Jamie Dornan has touched down in New Zealand, with fellow newcomer Kate Winslet also on the way.

The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum arrives in theaters on December 17, 2027. For more, check out our guide on how to watch all the Lord of the Rings movies in order, and keep up with upcoming movies heading your way.

#3957. Poll: What Do You Think The Metacritic Score Will Be For GTA 6?

Considering we're just a few days away from the release of GTA 6 on November 19th, we're bound to start getting reviews at some point between now and launch, and it'll be fascinating to see what the critics think of it!

This is a series that has consistently dominated on Metacritic over the years - a website that takes loads of professional reviews and creates an average score based around them. Grand Theft Auto V has a 97 average rating on there, for example, while GTA 4 goes even higher with a 98 rating.

In fact, every mainline release since GTA 3 (not including stuff like Chinatown Wars and Liberty City Stories) has reached at least a 95 on the platform. To put that into context, the best-rated Xbox Series X game of the year on Metacritic right now is Hades 2, and that game has a 95 average rating.

Feature These Are Xbox's Best 25 Games From 2001-2026 According To Metacritic

If we're going off history alone, GTA 6 has every chance of becoming the highest-reviewed game of 2026 on Xbox and PS5. The question is whether it'll manage to hit those highs once again, or whether it'll struggle to meet the hype.

Let's not forget there's never been a wait like this for a GTA game before, and while absence definitely does make the heart grow fonder, it also creates a sense of expectation that's extremely difficult to live up to.

We'll have to wait and see what happens! You'll find a review roundup on Pure Xbox ASAP, and it seems the smart bet is at least a 95 rating on Metacritic, although that's much easier said than achieved.

For reference, here are some other Metacritic scores from GTA games in the past:

Guide GTA 6 Release Times: All The Key Details Xbox Players Need To Know

What did you pick in the poll? Let us know down in the comments section below.

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

#3956. Yet Another PS5 Firmware Update Is Ready to Download Now as GTA 6 Approaches

Sony has issued another system software update for PS5, and if you want access to any online features, you'll be forced to download and install it.

Yes, this is a required update; it brings the firmware to version 26.07-14.23.00, and is a fairly small 1.3 GB.

What does it do, then? Well, as was the case with the last update, it has one solitary patch note:

The folks at PlayStation have been really cracking down hard on the console's security. This update comes about two weeks after the last, which was also about a fortnight removed from the previous one — an unusually speedy deployment.

This is for a couple of reasons. The first is that hackers have been jailbreaking the PS5 in new and faster ways, utilising generative AI tech to find workarounds and weaknesses in the console's software infrastructure.

Secondly, GTA 6 is on the verge of release.

This is pertinent because, well, it's GTA 6; it's very possible it'll be the biggest game launch of all time. In other words, there's a heightened risk that people will want to hack their PS5 and gain access to the game without paying.

Sony has been making it so that your console must have the latest firmware installed to even boot up GTA 6, and it's highly likely today's update will indeed be a necessity if you want to play the game. This theoretically minimises the risk of jailbreaking and piracy.

With the game now less than 48 hours away, Sony has sent out one more pre-launch security measure in its battle against hackers.
